Steph McGovern has opened up about leaving the BBC’s Breakfast programme ahead of her return to the broadcaster, revealing that she wanted to leave after almost a decade in the role.

The TV presenter was a frequent face on BBC Breakfast from 2011 until 2019 as the show’s main business presenter and occasional co-host. While she initially left the programme to go on maternity leave, she announced a month later that she would be leaving the BBC to join Channel 4.

Speaking about her exit seven years on, McGovern said that she decided to leave for good as she “didn’t want to do the hours anymore”.

open image in gallery Steph McGovern on 'BBC Breakfast' in 2012 ( BBC )

“It was relentless,” she told The Telegraph. “I did it for nearly 10 years, and I was always the girl out and about at 3am, in a hard hat and hi-vis somewhere.”

McGovern, who shares a six-year-old daughter with her girlfriend, went onto host the now-axed Steph’s Packed Lunch on Channel 4 and competed on Netflix’s Celebrity Bear Hunt – however, she is now heading back to the BBC to host art dealer competition The Big Deal with Steph McGovern on BBC Two.

Looking back at her time on BBC Breakfast, McGovern also addressed the reported investigation into allegations of bullying made against presenter Naga Munchetty.

Last year, the BBC was said to have investigated complaints of bullying made about Munchetty over a three-year period. The presenter was accused of bullying a female colleague at BBC Breakfast and making a sex joke off-air, according to The Sun. The outcome of the investigation is currently unknown.

Speaking about working on the show, McGovern said that the team was like her “family” and that she still talks to Munchetty as well as hosts Louise Minchin, Carol Kirkwood, Sally Nugent and Susanna Reid who “took me under their wing”.

open image in gallery Steph McGovern is now hosting ‘The Big Deal’ for BBC Two ( Alamy/PA )

As for allegations of bullying, McGovern said: “No, I didn’t see any of that. I mean, the editor changed by the time I left so I didn’t work under the one who is there now. But, look, people just love speculating about drama and, unfortunately, it’s quite boring in real life.”

Programme editor Richard Frediani, who took on the role in September 2019, was also accused of bullying – however, he was cleared of the claims in September last year.

Since McGovern left the programme, BBC Breakfast has seen a number of its high-profile presenters exit – including Louise Minchin in 2021, Dan Walker the following year and most recently, Rachel Burden.

Burden announced in July that she was leaving the show as it was scrapping its Sunday morning shows due to budget cuts. Later that month, Munchetty also revealed that she was leaving the show to take over from Burden on BBC Radio 5 Live’s breakfast show, saying that it had been a privilege to be a part of the team for the last 17 years. The BBC has not said that the bullying investigation was related to her exit.

The boss of JP Morgan has warned Chancellor John Healey against raising taxes on bank earnings, as the Government prepares its autumn Budget for October, reports suggest.

Jamie Dimon told Mr Healey in a phone call that higher taxes can result in jobs being driven elsewhere, citing a decline in finance roles in New York that he partly blamed on the city’s tax burden, according to the Financial Times.

He warned against a windfall levy on bank profits or wider tax rises on wealth, the newspaper reported, citing a person briefed on the conversation.

Mr Healey is reportedly due to have conversations with other bank executives in the coming days.

The influential chief executive of the US investment banking giant has previously sounded warnings against raising taxes on the industry and criticised the UK’s corporation tax surcharge for banks.

Some groups, including the Trades Union Congress (TUC), are calling for the Government to increase the windfall levy from the current rate of 3% to at least 8%, which it said would raise £9 billion for the Treasury over four years.

Earlier this month, Mr Dimon said in an interview for the Master Investor Podcast that he “always thought it was wrong”, adding: “JP Morgan did not damage the UK… I just thought it lacked principle to punish a company that had nothing to do with the crisis, and is still there 16-17 years later.”

Referring to the potential for the surcharge to be hiked, Mr Dimon said: “If the Government decides to do it then there’s nothing I can do, but it will over time cause decisions to be made that they may not like.”

“If you have an uncompetitive tax system, capital leaves your country and… goes to other countries”, he warned, referring to an exodus of companies from London’s stock markets in the past two years.

“I wouldn’t want to see that, if I was running a country,” he said, stressing that he wants “to see the UK thrive”.

open image in gallery John Healey will deliver his first Budget as Chancellor on October 28 (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA Wire )

Mr Healey will deliver his first Budget as Chancellor on October 28, following his appointment by Prime Minister Andy Burnham last month.

The former defence secretary is faced with the challenge of finding more money to fund Mr Burnham’s devolution priorities and increased defence spending, as well as new cost-of-living measures such as cutting VAT from energy bills and reducing business rates for pubs.

Experts, including the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Niesr), have warned Mr Healey that he will need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Mr Healey has promised plans would be “built on fiscal discipline” and meet the fiscal rules set by previous chancellor Rachel Reeves.

Foregoing luxuries such as "avocado toast" and practising frugal living could help you secure a financial cushion and retire early from work.

FIRE (Financial Independence, Retire Early), a money management strategy, is gaining more traction as the old rules are being left behind.

“The retirement age is increasing so people face having to work for more years and they’re living longer,” says Rajan Lakhani, personal finance expert and head of money at Plum.

“And now with the extra challenges Gen Z is facing with the cost-of-living crisis and high housing costs, there’s more of a momentum behind FIRE.”

open image in gallery FIRE (Financial Independence Retire Early) is currently getting more traction as the old rules are being torn up ( Alamy/PA )

But what does FIRE actually look like in the day-to-day? Here’s what you need to know about this retirement finance strategy…

What is the aim of FIRE?

“FIRE is all about maximising the amount of money saved and invested to achieve financial independence at an early retirement age, so you don’t have to carry on working into your 50s and 60s,” says Lakhani.

How do you calculate your FIRE?

“The typical way is to multiply your expected annual retirement expenses by 25 to give an achievable nest egg based on you withdrawing 4% a year,” he explains.

“For example, if you need 30,000 a year, your FIRE number would be £750,000 – and you need to account for compound interest, investment returns, state benefits and any housing assets.”

What are the different ways to achieve Lean FIRE, Fat FIRE and Barista FIRE?

Early retirement looks different to everybody and FIRE has three approaches.

“Lean FIRE is for people who have a frugal lifestyle and want an early minimalist retirement. They earn enough to cover costs but save aggressively to retire early,” explains Lakhani.

open image in gallery Early retirement looks different to everybody and FIRE has three approaches ( Alamy/PA )

“Fat FIRE is for people who want a higher standard of living and retirement, requires more wealth and a higher income.

“While Barista FIRE is a hybrid approach where you choose semi-retirement. Many people just want to continue working for the camaraderie and to keep some money coming in.”

What’s the best age to start FIRE?

The sooner you start, the better.

“Gen Z has the best opportunity to achieve this goal of retiring early, but it’s a big lifestyle sacrifice,” he warns.

“If early millennials in their 40s haven’t started by now, it’s going to be very difficult for them to retire early, but they might be able to achieve Barista FIRE.”

How does FIRE work in practice?

The old financial trope of giving up avocado toast can work for FIRE savers.

“They need to be ruthless about unnecessary expenditure like takeaways,” says Lakhani.

open image in gallery The old financial trope of giving up avocado toast can work for FIRE savers ( Alamy/PA )

“They must budget for essential costs – rental, bills and transport – see what’s remaining and then save 50-70% of that. They must track every penny, review bank statements, cancel unused subscriptions, dress and furnish cheaply and buy second hand.”

A mindset of success is also needed.

“They need to work hard and earn those promotions, or change jobs or start a side hustle,” he adds.

Is FIRE realistic for the average person?

The FIRE method is not for everyone.

“FIRE savers need mental discipline, be wholly committed and it helps to start really early,” says Lakhani. “These are people who can stick to their goals while seeing friends going out enjoying themselves.”

He adds, “A big part of it is also earning a higher income and making progress in their career, and not everyone is able to do that.”

How do I start being FIRE?

There are lots of tools available to make saving and investing easier.

“Our customers connect their bank account to us then our algorithm works out how much to save. They regularly tell us they didn’t realise they could save that much,” says Lakhani.

“Mortgage rate rises and increased food prices has made saving more of a challenge but then 4-5% interest rates on savings is a decent return.”

open image in gallery There are lots of tools available to make saving and investing easier ( PA )

The key is to make your money work harder.

“I would recommend maxing out tax-efficient vehicles like ISA and that you start investing,” suggests Lakhani.

“In your 20s, you get 15-20 years’ market growth. Shop around to find low-cost and commission-free providers, diversify investments and give yourself the time to go through market peaks and troughs.”

What are the downsides?

“The extreme sacrifice in the prime of life can be tough,” reflects Lakhani. “Also, who knows what your health is going to be like in 30 years? That sacrifice could be misplaced.

“Investments are also at the mercy of the markets and there will be changes to state rules around the benefits, tax and social care regulations.”

What are the benefits?

“The main benefit is the freedom to live longer and later on your own terms and not having to have the pressure of the daily grind,” concludes Plum’s Lakhani. “It gives people the opportunity to pursue their true passions.”

President Trump has blamed the appearance of swathes of dead grass at the National Mall on “vandals.”​

The accusation comes just weeks after the president began to allege that algae blooms and peeling pool lining in the waters of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool were the result of vandalism.​

On Truth Social, Trump shared an aerial image of the grass at the National Mall which appeared to have large, dead patches in the same area that he held his July 4 celebration.​

“Look what VANDALS did to the grass connecting the vandalized World War II Monument and the vandalized Reflecting Pool, which will be opened again, and better than ever, shortly,” Trump wrote on Sunday night. “Anybody who thinks the Reflecting Pool wasn’t vandalized should go back to Law School!”​

open image in gallery President Trump has blamed damage to the grass near the National Mall on vandals ( @RealDonaldTrump/Truth Social )

The spot, which is near Washington, D.C.’s World War II Memorial, played host to more than 400,000 people ahead of his July 4 speech, Trump has previously claimed.

​Footage from a livestreaming webcam taken during the July 4 celebrations and reviewed by The Associated Press showed a bandstand and a seating area covering the lawn that Trump says has been vandalized. ​

Photographs taken by the publication also showed workers removing the structures in the days after the speech, with brown grass being revealed under each.​

Trump has previously accused vandals of causing damage around Washington, D.C., most notoriously with the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, which has been the site of major renovations. ​

The president announced plans to have the pool refurbished and repainted an “American-flag blue” earlier this year.​

open image in gallery Trump has previously blamed green algae appearing in the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on vandals ( Getty )

However, after the pool was refilled, bright green algae blooms quickly began appearing in the water. The pool’s lining also began to peel away, with tourists spotting chunks of the lining floating on the water’s surface.​

Trump quickly began suggesting that vandals had slashed the pool lining and that they had even poured chemicals into the water.​

Amid the controversy, former Olympic canoeist David Hearn was arrested for allegedly vandalizing the pool, only for the charges against him to be dropped. ​

Trump later lashed out at Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, after she moved to drop charges against Hearn. ​

“I was disappointed in Jeanine Pirro. Really disappointed with Jeanine Pirro,” he told reporters in the Oval Office. “She folded like an umbrella.”​

Trump added, “I think she choked, because the judge was really vicious.”​

open image in gallery Trump has also hit out at Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, for dropping charges against an ex-Olympian who was accused of damaging the Reflecting Pool ( AFP/Getty )

A court filing to dismiss the charges states that the blue sealant began to peel “almost immediately” after work on the pool was finished in June. ​

The filing, from Pirro’s office, stated that the “damage was the result of a botched installation and not vandalism.”​

Trump has also complained about the numbers “86 47” appearing in the grass near the National Mall, which he cited while criticizing Pirro’s decision on Truth Social. ​

“To me, it was a pure case of VANDALISM, that included the grass, which had a big 86 47 emblazoned in giant letters on it, and other elements of the surrounding area,” Trump claimed. ​

News.title: I swapped my tablet for the reMarkable paper pure and I’m never looking back
News.content:
I hate to say it, but I’ve started to forget how to write. While there’s always been something so satisfying about putting pen to paper, it’s an art form I’ve lost over the years thanks to my switch to laptops and tablets. But digital notebooks are finally bringing the joys of writing back again.

They offer the intimacy of paper and pen, but with an endless supply of pages and no biro to think about. They even turn your handwriting into printed text that you can easily share. For years, reMarkable has led the charge in the digital notebook space, and it’s recently launched the reMarkable paper pure.

Launched in early May, the latest model joins the smaller paper pro move and larger paper pro to complete the remarkable line-up. Featuring an e-ink display, it lets you annotate documents, jot down notes and review presentations on the go. I’ve been putting the latest digital notebook to the test for weeks, and I think I’ve fallen in love with writing again.



open image in gallery ( reMarkable )

Design

The new reMarkable paper pure replaces the reMarkable 2, the previous black-and-white notebook from the company. Compared to the reMarkable 2, the new model is faster, so gestures are recognised more quickly and latency when writing is reduced. That’s important to give the impression that it’s as natural as using a regular pen which, after all, has no lag between touching the paper and the ink appearing.

The battery lasts a third longer than the reMarkable 2 as well. It has a noticeably different look, with the metallic bar on the left-hand edge replaced by a white frame that matches the display, giving the impression of being more inviting and immersive.

open image in gallery The new model is more compact and has a brighter screen ( David Phelan/The Independent )

The actual display is the same size, 10.3in, but reMarkable says it’s the crispest and whitest display yet from the company. Though the screen remains the same size, the new model is more compact, just 228mm tall instead of the reMarkable 2’s 246mm height, thanks to a much narrower bezel at the bottom. The front of the notebook is flush to the display throughout.

It’s thicker than its predecessor, perhaps to enable the 3,820mAh battery instead of the last model’s 3,000mAh cell. It still feels thin in the hand. And the weight has dropped, too, a full 43g lighter than the predecessor. The internal storage has increased from 8GB to 32GB.

One other change worth noting is the price. And it’s a good change: where the reMarkable 2 cost £389 with the basic Marker pen supplied, the new model costs £359. This makes it the most affordable notebook in the reMarkable range.

Since writing on the display is central to the device, the pencil is crucial. The reMarkable paper pure comes with the marker included, or you can upgrade to the marker plus (£40 extra) which has a different finish and a built-in eraser. Each snaps to the right edge of the paper pure magnetically, where it charges.

User experience

open image in gallery The slight resistance on the stylus feels like you’re writing on paper ( David Phelan/The Independent )

Using the marker is where you begin to see how different the paper pure is from a tablet. Where even the best stylus slides along the shiny glass of a tablet, here there’s a resistance that feels close to the reality of writing on paper. Of course, the screen doesn’t have the give of a paper pad, but the rough, matte finish of the display creates a resistance which means writing feels natural and controlled.

Mind you, it may remind you that your handwriting is especially spidery if you, like many of us, don’t write much by hand these days. Well, here’s a chance to improve.

And however bad your scrawl, the paper pure is good at turning it into printed text. If it makes a mistake, you can correct typos using an onscreen keyboard. When you convert from writing to text, it puts the words on a new page so your original handwriting remains untouched, unless you lasso your scribble with the selection tool, in which case it replaces it.

Unlike the other reMarkable notebooks, this one doesn’t have a front light, meaning that, like with real paper, you need light in the room to use it. On the other hand, because it uses E-ink, there’s no light shining in your eyes as there is with a regular tablet, which makes for a more restful experience.

There’s no doubt the interface is original, designed to be as distraction-free as possible, but it does mean there’s a learning curve, though it’s worth persevering with. Once you’ve got to grips with how to create notebooks, select writing to convert to text, correct inaccurate conversions and share documents, it all becomes second nature.

Features

open image in gallery The stylus becomes a ballpoint, pencil, paintbrush, highlighter and more ( David Phelan/The Independent )

The stylus can be used to switch from ballpoint to pencil, paintbrush to highlighter and more. Each flows differently, matching the effect you want to create, or your mood.

The display offers highlighter colours, though these only show up as grey on this device, obviously. You can mirror your display online, for others to see. The colour of the highlighter shows up there or on the other reMarkable models, which have colour displays.

Online you can also drop PDF and other files into your account and the file shows up instantly on the paper pure.

Collaboration has become an increasingly important part of the reMarkable experience, and as well as uploading notebooks you can link a calendar or share a document to others.

While features like Convert to Text are available free to all users, some advanced elements require a subscription, which costs £39 a year or £3.99 a month. These include handwriting search, extra templates and unlimited cloud storage.

Battery life

Since E-ink displays only consume energy when they refresh, the battery life of devices like this is measured in days rather than hours. It definitely lives up to reMarkable’s claim of almost three weeks between charges.

Key specifications

Display: 10.3-inch third-generation Canvas display, black-and-white

10.3-inch third-generation Canvas display, black-and-white Reading light: No

No Storage: 32GB

32GB Size: 228.1 x 187.1 x 6mm

228.1 x 187.1 x 6mm Weight: 360g

3,820mAh File formats: PDF, ePUB

Why we love it

Great build quality and design

Simplicity of purpose

Range of features

Take note

No reading light

Should you buy the reMarkable paper pure?

Using the reMarkable paper pure is a happy experience. The level of focus is way more than I can achieve from a tablet, and the elegant efficiency of stylus on electronic paper is satisfying. At first, there’s something daunting about the blank page, for sure, but the joy of distraction-free work is not to be underestimated.

Note-taking is simple and effective, with few corrections needed when converted into text – though making these changes can take a little patience. The effect of writing on the display may not be a perfect imitation of pen on paper, but it’s highly persuasive and enjoyable.

The light, thin build is appealing and the 10.3in display is attractive, inviting and just the right size. I miss the reading light from the paper pro, but it’s not a deal-breaker, and this device is significantly more affordable.

Some gadgets are marketed on the basis of their versatility. The strength of the paper pure is the simplicity of its purpose, and how adeptly that’s achieved.

Police near Manchester have ended a two-day stand-off by climbing a ladder to arrest the suspect who had fallen asleep on a roof.

Greater Manchester Police released footage showing the moment an officer climbed the ladder onto the roof of a back porch in Ash Street, Salford, and grabbed the man, who was lying down.

The man’s trousers appeared to fall as he was pulled down the ladder and arrested by officers in the garden of the property.

The force said two police officers suffered minor injuries during the incident on Saturday.

On Monday, a police spokesperson confirmed Simon Harris, 37, of no fixed address, was charged with four counts of criminal damage, two counts of assault of an emergency worker, intentionally/recklessly causing a public nuisance, burglary dwelling and theft.

He is due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates’ Court on Monday morning.

Detective Chief Inspector Helen Bagnall thanked members of the public following the man’s arrest, which came after a two-day emergency service response.

She said: “This was an extensive use of vital policing resources and clearly demonstrates the dangers our officers face on a daily basis in order to protect the people of Greater Manchester.

“Two of our officers suffered minor injuries during this incident.

“I would like to reiterate my thanks to the people of Salford for their patience and understanding whilst emergency service personnel dealt with this incident.”

News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

News.title: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
News.content:
Newcastle United 1 Bayer Leverkusen 2

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

News.title: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn
News.content:
Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Mowbray: It feels like a defeat

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

News.title: How to have the perfect slow-paced holiday in Zakynthos
News.content:
Zakynthos, also known as Zante, is renowned for raucous nightlife, but there’s a far more authentic side to the Venetians “Fiore di Levante” (Flower of the East). For such a small island, scenery is extremely varied: the southern coastline – home to Laganas’ notorious nightlife strip – also encompasses the pristine beaches of Zakynthos Marine Park, where loggerhead sea turtles come to nest, while some of the island’s best-known attractions, including Navagio Beach on the cliff-lined northerly coast, can only be reached by boat.

Birthplace of the man who penned Greece’s national anthem, Zakynthos was also a magnet for literary greats: Byron lay in state here and philhellene Edgar Allan Poe wrote a sonnet to the island’s “verdant slopes”.

Last but not least, food is a powerful lure here: sit in a rustic sea view tavern sipping local Verdea white wine with a plate full of traditional kouneli stifado – a garlic and tomato-soaked rabbit stew – and you’ll be hooked.

News.title: Ebola doctors ‘step back’ from WHO in drug trial ethics row
News.content:
Two leading doctors have “stepped back” from long-held positions with the World Health Organization amid a row over the ethics of an Ebola drug trial underway in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The randomised control trial, called Ebo-Pep, is testing whether an experimental antiviral is an effective post-exposure treatment.

But experts believe the study’s design puts healthcare workers on the frontline of the epidemic at risk, because it means medics exposed to Ebola might receive a placebo treatment.

“We owe them [healthcare workers] a duty of care to do the best possible thing, and a 50 per cent chance of getting a placebo tablet is not that,” said Prof Tom Fletcher, director of the Global Health Trials Unit at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine. The WHO’s health emergencies clinical unit has also deployed him to Ebola ‘Red Zones’ for more than a decade.

This week, Prof Fletcher and eight other experts based in the UK, US, Uganda, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Canada published their concerns in Nature Africa, calling for a “careful reconsideration” of the trial protocol.

They said they are not against Ebo-Pep or randomised trials, but warned there are “additional ethical obligations” when including healthcare workers in studies like this, given the case fatality rate currently stands at 40 per cent.

Prof Fletcher said: “Ebo-Pep is a really good trial, it’s the trial we’ve talked about doing for years. But we’re talking about [protecting] the ‘one-per-centers’, the people who willingly step into one of the most dangerous environments in the world.”

News.title: Wildfire watch: Inside London’s fire control centre on the hottest day of the year
News.content:
“It’s been relentless, an immense number of calls,” says Yvonne Woodhams, control room commander at the London Fire Brigade’s headquarters on the morning of what turned out to be the hottest day of the year so far.

Inside a nondescript building in South-west London, dozens of fire brigade dispatchers field calls from the public and direct the city’s 5,000 or so firefighters across 102 stations to where they are most needed.

In the middle of another heatwave and on a day when temperatures rose to just above 38 degrees, the control room was busy – the scale and frequency of wildfires in London’s parks and grasslands are now considered unprecedented.

Above the dispatchers there is a live map, with red dots representing each active fire, sprawling from Enfield in the north to Purley in the south.

Wildfires nearly always have a human origin like dropped cigarette butts, glass bottles that magnifies the sunlight, or the now-temporarily banned portable barbecues.

But it’s the tinderbox that London has become which is worrying firefighters.

Scorching hot, low-humidity weather, a bit of wind, and tinder-dry vegetation can cause the smallest spark to ignite an inferno. Conditions like this have been described as “fire weather” by the author John Vaillant.

The England winger made his maiden outing for his new club over the weekend following his blockbuster £69million move from Newcastle.

Sports.title: Adorable reason why Cristiano Ronaldo married Georgina Rodriguez on August 11 with date holding very special meaning

Ronaldo, 41, and Georgina, 32, finally tied the knot after a ten-year relationship that saw them getting engaged in 2025.

The Al-Nassr captain and the content creator met at a Gucci store in Madrid where she worked while he played for Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez’s Juventus transfer collapses despite Aston Villa signing £30million replacement for Argentine
Sports.content:
JUVENTUS’ move for Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has fallen apart despite the Premier League club already lining up his replacement.

The Argentine goalkeeper and former World Cup winner has been heavily linked with an exit for the past two summers.



Italian giants Juventus finally seemed set to give him a new home after approaching Villa with a number of bids for the 33-year-old’s services this window.

But now The Athletic have reported that the Bianconeri have decided to move on and pursue other targets after failing to agree a deal for the stopper.



That leaves Martinez in an awkward spot, with Villa already having a deal in place for his replacement Zion Suzuki.

The Japanese World Cup star seemed set to join French champions Paris Saint-Germain earlier this window.



But Villa pounced after that deal fell through late on, agreeing a deal with Parma that could be worth up to £30million.

He is set to arrive on a five-year contract.

The 23-year-old is understood to be the club’s first-choice for the upcoming season regardless of Martinez’s transfer status.

But with Villa set to compete in the Champions League this season, squad depth is on the agenda, and the two-time Yashin award winner would likely get some opportunity to play if he ended up as back-up this season.

Sports.title: Neymar’s bitter rival refuses to shake his hand as feud rages on SIX YEARS after pair first clashed
Sports.content:
FOE REAL Neymar’s bitter rival refuses to shake his hand as feud rages on SIX YEARS after pair first clashed

NEYMAR renewed his heated feud with bitter rival Thiago Mendes, who refused to shake his hand just before kick-off, this past weekend.

The Santos superstar returned to action in the Brazilian Serie A after retiring from Brazil following his last World Cup in July.



The star forward led his team on Sunday when they visited Vasco at Sao Januario in the league when tensions grew between him and Mendes, 34.

During the pre-match handshakes, the Barcelona legend greeted everyone but was ultimately snubbed by his rival.



Mendes didn’t accept a handshake from the 34-year-old, who was left smiling awkwardly before proceeding to greet the referees.

Their feud dates back in 2020 when Neymar played for Paris Saint-Germain.

Everything began during a Ligue 1 match when Mendes – then a Lyon ace – injured his fellow Brazilian.

The midfielder committed a late challenge that led to Neymar being stretchered off in tears.

Mendes was sent off after a VAR review and later received a three-match ban.

Neymar was diagnosed with a sprained ankle and was sidelined for about a month.



The Brazil legend’s father Neymar Santos Sr took to social media where he put Mendes on full blast.

The defensive midfielder, who apologised online, then claimed he and his family received threats and abuse following the incident.

Their rivalry was rekindled six years later this past February during Santos‘ 2-1 win at Vila Belmiro.

Neymar was enraged after a foul committed against him and confronted Mendes in the first half.

Shortly afterward, the pair began arguing until the ex-PSG star fell to the ground after the Vasco ace touched his face.



Both were shown yellow cards and kept arguing throughout the heated match that then saw Neymar bringing up the foul that led to his injury in France.

He said: “He always wants to start trouble, he always wants to act tough, it’s always like that.

“With all due respect, he’s an idiot. He already hurt me once at PSG, he threatened me today, so let’s see if he’s man enough to hurt me again.”

Neymar had the last laugh yesterday as he led Santos to a 3-0 victory against his bitter rival.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy ‘offered transfer to Brazilian giants Sao Paulo’ as former club Sheffield Wednesday seek emotional return
Sports.content:
CLUBLESS Jamie Vardy has been approached by Brazilian club Sao Paulo as his search for a new team goes on.

The Leicester legend is still assessing his options, with several English clubs also circling for his signature.



Italian reporter Fabrizio Romano was the first to break the news of Sao Paulo’s interest.

But the Englishman is reportedly still considering his options.



The Brazilian club’s approach could come as an unwanted surprise to Vardy‘s former club Sheffield Wednesday.

The Yorkshire club would love to reunite with their former player, following relegation to League One.

Wednesday’s new chairman David Storch recently revealed he would like to bring Vardy home to his boyhood club.

Vardy has drawn interest from a host of clubs, including West Ham as they begin their battle in the Championship.

The 39-year-old has been a free agent since departing then-Serie A side Cremonese at the end of June, after scoring seven goals in 29 games.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta warns Arsenal’s rivals they’re out to ‘win everything’ after demolishing Man City in Community Shield
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA warned that Arsenal proved their hunger for back-to-back Premier League titles by demolishing Manchester City.

Riccardo Calafiori scored after just 23 seconds in Cardiff then the Gunners added two more goals through Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard.



Skipper Odegaard said the champions “showed our level” and “want to win everything.”

Arsenal have never previously lifted successive Prem crowns.



But Arteta insists: “We know that it is going to demand something special – and we are going to go for it.

“The desire comes with saying ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to live other moments even bigger than that’.

“There is more belief, we know how to do it, what it takes to win it, that was the biggest asset of the team. To play in the manner we did is extremely impressive.”

Arsenal ended the club’s 22-year wait to win the league last season and came agonisingly close to adding the Champions League – losing the final to PSG on penalties.

Skipper Odegaard said: “We showed our level. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

Several of Arteta’s players only reported back for pre season training this week but he said they were desperate to play.

Sports.title: Chelsea legend backs experienced veteran duo Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to TRANSFORM Xabi Alonso’s Blues
Sports.content:
CHELSEA legend Ruud Gullit believes Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck can transform the Blues.

When superstar Gullit came to Stamford Bridge in 1995, a few months shy of his 33rd birthday, it marked the beginning of a new era for the club.



And the Dutchman says thirtysomethings Henderson and Welbeck bring the experience and authority Chelsea’s otherwise young squad has needed for so long.

Gullit said: “It’s funny. We spent so much time discussing how Chelsea lacked experience, and now they’ve added pure experience.



“Their previous issue was a complete lack of veteran presence.

“Henderson and Welbeck will be crucial in the dressing room and on the training pitch.



“They can advise younger players on what mistakes to avoid.

“Their impact isn’t just measured by matchday minutes, it’s what they do during the week.

“You need that guidance in a squad, so the signings make total sense.”

Chelsea fans spent much of last season slamming the owners and recruitment chiefs for their policy of signing mainly young players.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

6 Stamford Bridge supremo Behdad Eghbali pledged to bring in “ready-made” players to complement talent like teenage sensation Estevao.

Henderson, 36, won everything as captain of Liverpool, while Welbeck, 35, has been a Premier League striker for nearly 18 years.

Yet some Chelsea supporters are not convinced the pair are the right men to revive the club’s fortunes.

But Gullit gives BlueCo credit for recognising their mistakes and reckons Henderson and Welbeck, along with new manager Xabi Alonso, can make a real difference.

Gullit said: “The new ownership had a vision, but it failed in execution because they arrived with zero background or experience in football.

“American sports management models don’t translate directly to European football.



“They initially thought they could win exclusively with young prospects. But who guides those players when things go wrong?

“On the pitch, they looked frantic and hasty – always playing in fifth gear without any composure or ability to dictate the tempo.

“Now, appointing a manager with a strong footballing background and adding experienced players shows they are finally adjusting their philosophy.



“To win trophies, you must balance youth with experienced leaders who can guide young players.”

Gullit became Chelsea’s player-manager when Glenn Hoddle left to boss England in 1996.

The Dutchman led a team featuring Gianfranco Zola, Gianluca Vialli and Roberto di Matteo to FA Cup triumph in his first season in charge.

But Gullit was sacked in February 1998, despite the Blues enjoying another successful campaign, being following rows with then chairman Ken Bates.

Alonso is Chelsea’s SIXTH permanent boss since the BlueCo takeover in May 2022.



But Blues chiefs have vowed to give the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen head coach time to make an impact – and have given him the title of “manager” to reflect his greater influence over recruitment and the club overall.

Gullit, speaking on behalf of NY Sports Day, said: “Alonso will want to prove himself after how things ended at Real Madrid.

“He has all the qualities to be a top manager, and he brings that experience with him to London.

“Initially, I was sceptical about why he chose Chelsea given their rigid structure of handing a manager a squad and telling him to deal with it.

“But it feels as though Alonso insisted on having a direct say in recruitment before accepting the job.



“The board appears to be listening to him now rather than dictating policy.

“It won’t happen overnight – he needs time to evaluate a very large squad and establish his core group.”

Sports.title: Barcelona AGREE £65.4million Rodri transfer hours after Enzo Maresca pleaded with Man City owners to make signings
Sports.content:
BARCELONA have agreed a deal worth £65.4 million for Manchester City midfielder Rodri.

The Catalan giants had seen previous bids for the 30-year-old former Ballon d’Or winner thrown out by the Prem club.



However within a couple of hours of the final whistle in the Community Shield, they struck a verbal agreement which will see them pay around £51m upfront.

And City are sure the add ons will take the fee they receive way beyond the £60m mark.



They believe it is a good deal for Rodri who has just 10 months left on his deal and has struggled with injuries over the last two years.

Maresca said in Cardiff that his team need new signings as quickly as possible after they were well beaten by Arsenal.



And they will step up the hunt for a new holding midfielder with Rodri’s move to Spain now set to be finalised in the next 48 hours.

A move for Morocco World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi is advanced with Lille demanding around £85 million for the teen ace.

However they will look for a direct replacement for Rodri who has spent the last seven years at the club and scored the winner in the Champions League final in 2023.

Record signing Elliot Anderson is the only new face likely to feature regularly for the first team and Maresca says there is still work to be done on the squad.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The ex-Chelsea boss said: “With any new signing, the sooner they arrive the better because we are starting the Premier League in one week.

“If they start to work with us as soon as possible it’s better that they can also understand the way we want to play.

“We knew already before the game of the things that we need to do.

“It’s not because we lost the game or even if we had won the game to think differently.



“We are quite clear in what we need to do and for sure we are going to do something before the window closes.”

There was no sign of Rodri in South Wales as talks with Barcelona continued and his absence sparked speculation a deal could be close.

The City boss said: “Rodri is a player who just won the World Cup and Ballon d’Or. He’s a top player, all the teams need Rodri so it’s not about if we miss him or not.

“The ones that played today – Elliot was quite good on his first game.”

There was also a first City appearance in 15 months for England international Jack Grealish who came on as a second half sub.



The ex Aston Villa captain is still expected to leave this month but Maresca said: “Overall I think Jack was good.

“The ones that are still here and want to work every day and if they deserve they’re going to get minutes.”

Skipper Ruben Dias admitted his team will need time to get used to life under the new boss after 10 years of playing for Pep Guardiola.

The Portugal international said: “The feeling is there’s a lot of work to put in. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working.



“There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.”

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim 'feels nothing' for Man Utd after perfect reunion following horror stint
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim 'feels nothing' for Man Utd after perfect reunion following horror stint

Ruben Amorim insists his emotional attachment to Manchester United has gone after his AC Milan side got the better of the Premier League team in pre-season

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim got one over on his former side as AC Milan beat Man Utd

Ruben Amorim insists he "feels nothing for Manchester United" after getting the better of his former club in a pre-season clash at the weekend.

‌



The Portuguese coach was axed by the Red Devils in January but hired by AC Milan this summer - and the pre-season schedule saw the two sides meet in Poland at the weekend. Milan would secure a 4-2 win as Amorim got one over on his former team.

‌



The Italians had struggled in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Chelsea recently as Amorim found it difficult to have the impact he'd hoped for, but he landed a much needed win against the Premier League giants.

‌



Despite the build-up Amorim insists there was no added emotion when it came to facing United, where his tenure ended with him winning just 24 of his 63 matches, as the ex-Sporting Lisbon boss insists he feels nothing for them despite his previous connection.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Amorim told Sky Sport Italia: "No. For me, it was just a normal match. Since I signed with Milan, I've felt nothing about Manchester United. I'm just proud to have been at Man United and I still love the club, but after signing with Milan, I [feel] nothing bad about anything because I'm very happy, because I'm in the place where I want to be. I just want to continue here.

‌



"Of course, it was special to play against them again, but I wanted to win a game this preseason to present ourselves well in our league, to give a good image to our fans, so they can support us in our first match."

Amorim was appointed in November 2024 and would go on to preside over the club's worst ever Premier League finish, ending in 15th during a season that saw them win just 11 times. He would also lose in the Europa League final before his dismissal the following year.

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim endured a nightmare spell in Manchester (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

‌



Despite his Manchester struggles Amorim still landed the top job at one of Europe's most decorated sides and apologised to United upon his unveiling.

"It is hard to explain the mistakes as I would have to explain all the context of the last adventure," he said. "The only thing I can say is that I learn a lot and I did some mistakes.

"I didn't have [the] opportunity - and I am sorry for that - to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment [but] I am really proud to have been their coach for a year."

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Rodri £65.4m latest, Liverpool's Barcola boost, Osimhen to Arsenal
Sports.content:
All of the latest transfer news from the Premier League and further afield, including updates on Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester United, Tottenham and more

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's transfer live blog for Monday, August 16.

The big news on Sunday night is that Rodri is poised to join Barcelona in a deal worth £65.4m. Manchester City had hoped Rodri would sign a new contract at the Etihad, but with his deal entering the final year, it became clear the Ballon d'Or winner would not commit. He is now set to undergo a medical before signing a four-year contract with the Spanish giants.

While Lille remain in talks with a number of clubs over their Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi. City are one of the clubs in talks with the Ligue 1 side regarding a deal for Bouaddi as they replenish their midfield.

Liverpool’s hopes of signing Bradley Barcola also received a boost on Sunday after he was left out of the Paris Saint-Germain squad for the French Super Cup final against Lens. That development comes after PSG completed the signing of Spain's World Cup final hero Ferran Torres from Barcelona for £42.7m.

The French giants also secured the signing of Mika Godts from Ajax over the weekend. The deal could be worth up to €55million (£47m; $63.63m) to Ajax, consisting of an initial fee of €45m, plus €10m in potential add-ons.

Arsenal, meanwhile, may have to fork out at least £60m if they hope to sign Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen before next month's transfer deadline. The Gunners are looking to add firepower to their attack this summer, having missed out on Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior following a long and drawn-out transfer saga.

Stay tuned for all of the latest news and updates in our transfer blog below...

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta 'fighting' to change Premier League rule that would suit Arsenal
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta 'fighting' to change Premier League rule that would suit Arsenal

Mikel Arteta wants to see the Premier League change the rule regarding the amount of substitutes he can name as he lamented the fact he had to leave out some of his Arsenal stars and teenage prospects

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta led Arsenal to an impressive win in Cardiff

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admits he's fighting with the Premier League to increase the amount of subs available on matchdays as he bemoaned the fact he had to leave out some of his players.

‌



The Gunners began their season with a statement win as the Premier League champions downed last year's domestic cup winners Manchester City 3-0 in Cardiff, taking the lead within 30 seconds before asserting their dominance.

‌



Arteta was able to showcase the strength of his squad with Martin Odegaard taking centre stage, but plenty of talk was surrounding the names he didn't name in the starting IX or on the bench, fuelling suggestions they will be on the moved before the transfer window closes.

‌



Teenage star Ethan Nwaneri was among those to be left out with Noni Madueke, Odegaard, new signing Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz named as the team's four attacking players. Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze, Max Dowman and Viktor Gyokeres were among the substitutes.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And Arteta confessed he wants to see the rules over bench numbers tweaked as he said to TNT Sports: “It’s really sad not to have their availability. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend and accommodate more players in the squad because they deserve to be in the squad, there’s no question.

‌



“Ethan [Nwaneri] and Marli [Salmon] as well, who has had the whole pre-season with us. Hopefully we can change that rule so players can enjoy on the pitch and can be an option to play and contribute to the team going forward.”

Brazilian duo Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli were among those not included in Sunday’s clash. Jesus only has a year left on his deal at the Emirates whilst Martinelli is of interest to Galatasaray and is ultimately competing in one of the most competitive parts of the squad.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are both linked with the exit door (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



When asked if they will remain Arsenal players in this transfer window, Arteta replied: “Yes they’re very important for us.”

Arsenal's bench also included England talisman Declan Rice, who will come back into the starting XI, and Spain's World Cup winners Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi among the internationals Arteta could call upon.

Arteta has been able to assemble arguably Europe's most impressive squad during his tenure at Arsenal, giving them huge depth and quality. Those lower down the Premier League, who will have to try and find a way to thwart the champions this season, will no doubt argue that increasing the sub numbers would only give the top sides an even greater advantage.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Barcola alternative sends message to Iraola as transfer plan clarified
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Barcola alternative sends message to Iraola as transfer plan clarified

Liverpool begin their Premier League campaign against Newcastle United in six days but their hunt for a new winger continues

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has less than a week until his first Premier League game as Liverpool boss (Image: Getty)

Liverpool now have less than a week until their Premier League campaign begins. But Andoni Iraola's side have only welcomed in three senior signings so far.

‌



This summer has been a relatively quiet one for the Reds. With the Iraola era underway, filling the void left by Ibrahima Konate's free transfer to Real Madrid has led the club to recruit two new centre-backs.

‌



Jeremy Jacquet has arrived from Rennes for £60million following negotiations in January and Ronald Araujo will likely partner Virgil van Dijk to begin the season after he signed on a one-year loan deal from Barcelona. The Uruguayan can be bought after his loan spell for £47.1m.

‌



Bradley Barcola has emerged as Liverpool's top target as they look to bolster their attacking arsenal, but their third summer addition, Victor Munoz, could ease any concerns. Mirror Football has a look at the latest updates out of Anfield.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool learn new PSG decision on Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye after transfer announcement READ MORE :

Liverpool finally change transfer stance after breakthrough in negotiations READ MORE :

Victor Munoz sends a message

The tail end of this transfer window appears set to be dominated by Liverpool's pursuit of Barcola. With Mohamed Salah now playing for Trabzonspor, a new superstar winger has been sought out and the Frenchman fits the bill.

‌



View 3 Images Munoz was the best player on the pitch for the Reds (Image: Getty)

However, as things stand, PSG's £130m asking price is out of Liverpool's price range. Not to mention, Barcola primarily plays off the left, whereas a right-winger is what the Reds really desire.

Munoz might have something to say about this, though. He has proved he can play a big role under Iraola. Liverpool faced Italian side Como twice on Sunday, with the first friendly taking place behind closed doors at AXA Training Centre. Munoz was the star of the show.

‌



The World Cup winner, who was signed from Osasuna for £34.6m in June, started on the left wing and was a danger from minute one. He tore Como right-back Ivan Smolcic to shreds and was taken off in the 46th minute of what was only a 70-minute match.

Munoz was so impressive that Iraola may need to reassess whether a player like Barcola is necessary. The French star likes it off the left and with Rio Ngumoha saying he's getting used to playing on both flanks, an alternative may already be at the club in the form of Munoz.

‌



Curtis Jones transfer plan

Munoz's team-mate Curtis Jones seems set to leave Liverpool this summer. He has been a target for Inter Milan for some time now, with Iraola preferring other options in the middle of the park.

Liverpool's £34m demand has so far proved too pricey for Inter, who have shifted midfield star Davide Frattesi to Lazio to free up wages and space.

View 3 Images Jones' future is uncertain (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

But now, reports in Italy suggest another midfielder will soon be sold, finally enabling them to scoop up Jones. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Luis Henrique, formerly of Marseille, is now on the chopping block.

When he is sold, Inter will move for the Liverpool midfielder. It is claimed that Roma are one of the few clubs interested in talking Henrique off Inter's hands.

Sports.title: Jeremy Jacquet scores on Liverpool debut as Cody Gakpo sends reminder - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Jeremy Jacquet scores on Liverpool debut as Cody Gakpo sends reminder - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 2-0 COMO: Goals from Cody Gakpo and Jeremy Jacquet ended pre-season on a high for the Reds, with Andoni Iraola getting another look at his squad at Anfield

View 5 Images Liverpool paid £60million to sign Jeremy Jacquet (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Liverpool rounded out pre-season with a comfortable 2-0 win against Cesc Fabregas' Como. New signing Jeremy Jacquet was among the goals, while Cody Gakpo opened the scoring amid uncertainty over his future.

‌



Andoni Iraola's side head to Newcastle next Sunday, so it was a final chance for the new Reds boss to get a look at his players in action. Ronald Araujo also made his first appearance for Liverpool since joining on a season-long loan from Barcelona.

‌



A quirk of this fixture was that the two teams had already played each other in a behind-closed-doors game earlier in the day. It finished 0-0 at Liverpool's AXA Training Centre, with Alexis Mac Allister the notable inclusion.

‌



Here are five talking points from Anfield.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



1. Jones absent again amid Inter interest

When team news was released, all eyes were on whether Curtis Jones would make his return to the Liverpool squad. But the midfielder was missing for the second game running, with his future on Merseyside uncertain.

Italian giants Inter Milan are preparing a new bid for Jones, who's reportedly keen on the move to San Siro. Liverpool say that the 25-year-old has been dealing with a hip problem and trained alone on Sunday.

Where will Liverpool finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images Inter Milan want to sign the injured Curtis Jones (Image: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

2. Gakpo sends timely reminder

Another player who's been linked with an exit is Gakpo. Tottenham are understood to be pushing to sign the Netherlands international, with reports claiming that personal terms have already been agreed.

But Gakpo has remained professional and finished off a flowing move to break the deadlock on 23 minutes. Jeremie Frimpong drove inside from right-back and lifted the ball over Como's defence.

‌



Gakpo controlled it well and slotted home in one motion, sending a reminder to the Reds of what they'd be losing if they sell him to Tottenham. With Mo Salah gone, can Liverpool afford to lose another established forward?

View 5 Images Cody Gakpo is a target for Tottenham (Image: Darren Staples/AFP via Getty Images)

3. Jacquet's good first impression

With half-time looming, Como looked the more likely to score after a decent spell. But it was Liverpool who ended up doubling their lead before the interval.

‌



Jacquet - making his first appearance of pre-season after recovering from a knee injury - was the scorer, given a simple tap-in from Gakpo's low cross. It was a gift for the centre-back, who's had to be patient to get his chance.

There was more to Jacquet's performance than his goal, though. The former Rennes prospect was enjoying himself defensively; showing composure on the ball, putting in challenges and made a goal-saving tackle shortly before his strike.

Jacquet was replaced at half-time, as Araujo made his Anfield bow. Lewis Koumas - who'd played 25 minutes in the earlier game - was also introduced, coming on for Rio Ngumoha.

‌



View 5 Images Jeremy Jacquet scored a goal - and prevented one (Image: Darren Staples/AFP via Getty Images)

4. The Wirtz conundrum

When Liverpool shelled out a then-club-record £116million to sign Florian Wirtz a year ago, it was expected that he'd be rocking and rolling by now. But something still hasn't clicked.

The ex-Bayer Leverkusen star showed plenty of neat touches but didn't cause Como enough problems with his passing or dribbling. Fans are starting to doubt whether Wirtz deserves a starting berth, especially with Mac Allister on the verge of a return.

‌



Given time, one would expect his partnership with Alexander Isak to bear fruit. For now, though, perhaps pushing Dominik Szoboszlai further forward is a right call.

View 5 Images Florian Wirtz is a concern for Andoni Iraola (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

5. Next stop: St James' Park

So that's that. Liverpool's 2026 pre-season campaign is complete. The Reds have come away with three wins, two defeats and one draw from their six friendlies.

‌



Now the focus is on facing Newcastle, who've had a summer of change of their own. Iraola has a few selection headaches before next Sunday's visit to Tyneside, but could he have Bradley Barcola at his disposal?

Liverpool's top target remains at Paris Saint-Germain player and is valued at £145m. But with the transfer window closing in just over two weeks, PSG could be tempted to budge.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher tells Man City to call off transfer immediately after Arsenal drubbing
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher tells Man City to call off transfer immediately after Arsenal drubbing

Arsenal dominated Manchester City as they beat Enzo Maresca's side 3-0 in the Community Shield at the Principality Stadium on Sunday afternoon

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher sent a transfer message to Manchester City during their Community Shield defeat to Arsenal (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Jamie Carragher has told Manchester City they must keep Rodri after watching Arsenal run riot in the Community Shield. The Gunners set a marker for the new season with a comfortable 3-0 victory over Enzo Maresca’s side in Cardiff.

‌



But new City boss Maresca omitted Rodri and Savinho as transfer speculation continues to surround them. Even though City have stated they want Rodri to stay and sign a new deal, it has become clear that he wants to leave, with Barcelona his preferred destination.

‌



The Catalan giants stepped up their interest in the midfielder earlier this week by making a second bid worth more than £51million. But as previously reported, City are asking for at least £70m for the World Cup winner.

‌



But as Carragher watched Maresca’s side come up short against the Premier League champions, the former Liverpool defender made clear he thinks that City need to cancel any talks to let Rodri leave. Taking to X, he wrote: “Arsenal 3-0. Man City have to keep Rodri.”

However, shortly after Carragher's post, Fabrizio Romano claimed that the Spaniard is closing in on a move to Barcelona after City 'gave the green light' to their latest offer.

On Sunday, Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after just 24 seconds for the Gunners before Kai Havertz added a second with a close-range header. Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard then wrapped up the win with a clever finish just three minutes after the break.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Rodri has entered the final 12 months of his City deal, and speaking in his pre-Arsenal press conference, Maresca updated on the Spaniard’s future, saying 'anything can happen' as long as the transfer window is open.

‌



And speaking after his side’s defeat at the Principality Stadium, the new City boss said: "I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment.

View 2 Images Man City were well beaten as Arsenal lifted the Community Shield (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

“I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated."

‌



He added: "We have many things to work [on]. The season's just started so there are many things we need to do better but even when we win games there are things we need to do better."

Sports.title: World Cup final referee's unheard plea to Lionel Messi exposed in new footage
Sports.content:
World Cup final referee's unheard plea to Lionel Messi exposed in new footage

Spain prevailed in a fiery World Cup final where referee Slavko Vincic pleaded with Lionel Messi over some of Argentina's second-half antics in the United States

View 2 Images Referee Slavko Vincic speaks to Lionel Messi during the World Cup final (Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu via Getty Images)

World Cup referee Slavko Vincic pleaded with Lionel Messi to calm down his out-of-control team-mate Leandro Paredes during the tournament's final. The Argentina captain was tasked with keeping Paredes on the field before the violent scenes he sparked come the full-time whistle.

‌



Paredes spotted kicking and punching as he shoved Spain star Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Barcelona ace Gavi. The 32-year-old only entered the match at half-time, but was fortunate to stay on the pitch.

‌



The former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder picked up a yellow card after just six minutes on the pitch for a nasty foul and spent the remainder of the match living on the edge as Enzo Fernandez was sent off. Paredes' antics prompted on-field official Vincic to attempt to take mitigating action through Messi, though that did not prevent the shenanigans at full time.

‌



Footage has emerged from referee cam in which Vincic can be heard warning Messi that Paredes was riding his luck on the field. "Messi, control Paredes," he could be heard saying.

"I don't want to...he has yellow. Control please. Always, always."

Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing READ MORE :

FIFA opened disciplinary proceedings against Paredes for his shameful post-match actions. The world football governing body has alleged three counts of assault against the player.

‌



Argentina's Nahuel Molina has also come under the spotlight for two counts of assault and team coach Roberto Ayala for one count. Molina appeared to strike Rodri while Ayala hit Dani Olmo.

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente was left in disbelief with what transpired. "At the time, I didn't realise it. I was celebrating, hugging team-mates," De La Fuente told Spanish television.

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes has been charged by FIFA due to the incident after the World Cup final vs Spain (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed. Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.

"I want to highlight our behaviour in the face of that kind of aggression and provocation. Our players always kept their composure and behaved like true professionals."

‌



Paredes was caught up in more drama upon his return to club football. The veteran sparked more uproar for Boca Juniors when he kicked the ball at an opponent.

As a Central Cordoba player looked to get to his feet following a foul, Paredes kicked the ball towards him, though how deliberate it was remains up for debate. Paredes was only on the field for 14 minutes.

Sports.title: All you need to know about the US Open Tennis - live on Sky Sports!
Sports.content:
When is the US Open? Does Jack Draper need to qualify for the US Open? Is Emma Raducanu playing? Who will win at Flushing Meadows? Key questions ahead of the last Grand Slam of 2026 - watch live from August 30 - September 13 on Sky Sports Tennis.

The final tennis Grand Slam of the year is nearly here, and you can watch all the action exclusively live on Sky Sports.

From Sunday August 30 to Sunday September 13, Sky Sports is your home for all the action from Flushing Meadows, when the stars come out to play.

Image: Watch the US Open from Flushing Meadows in Queen's New York

However, this year, qualifying week will welcome the return of the Mixed Doubles event which is set to see doubles specialists and top singles players compete for the title - including Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic.

There will also be a host of British talent across the women's singles, men's singles, doubles and wheelchair tennis draws.

How and where to watch US Open 2026 on Sky Sports

The final Grand Slam of the year will once again be broadcast exclusively live on Sky Sports Tennis, with any match available via Sky Sports+.

Sky Sports Tennis can be found on the linear channel number 407, while Sky Sports+ is number 410 for Sky Glass customers, 412 for Sky Q customers and 416 for customers in the Republic of Ireland.

You can also head to the 'Watch' section on the Sky Sports app to access all Sky Sports+ live streams via the event centres.

Don't have a subscription? No problem. You can also stream the US Open on Sky Sports Tennis and more live sport with a NOW Sports Day or Month Membership. No contract options are available.

Across Sky Sports' channels, as well as our digital and social channels, tennis fans can enjoy extensive coverage of the final Grand Slam of 2025, including both the men's and women's singles, alongside the respective doubles tournaments, mixed doubles, juniors, and wheelchair competitions.

There will be a daily live text commentary on the Sky Sports app and website, as well as live scores, reports, analysis, features and videos.

US Open schedule - live on Sky Sports

Image: Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, holds up the championship trophy after defeating Jannik Sinner, of Italy, in the men's singles final of the U.S. O

Monday, August 24 - Mixed doubles qualifying

Tuesday, August 25 - Mixed doubles - first & second rounds

Wednesday, August 26 - Mixed doubles - semi-finals & final

Thursday, August 27 - Qualifying

Sunday, August 30 - Men's & Women's singles 1st round

Tuesday, September 1 - Men's & Women's singles 1st round

Wednesday, September 2 - Men's & Women's singles 2nd round

Thursday, September 3 - Men's & Women's singles 2nd round, Women's doubles 1st round

Friday, September 4 - Men's & Women's singles 3rd round, Men's & Women's doubles 1st round

Saturday, September 5 - Men's & Women's singles 3rd round, Women's doubles 2nd round, Men's doubles 1st round

Sunday, September 6 - Men's & Women's singles 4th round, Men's & Women's doubles 2nd round

Tuesday, September 8 - Men's & Women's singles quarter-finals, Women's doubles quarter-finals, Men's doubles 3rd round, Wheelchair & Quad doubles quarter-finals

Wednesday, September 9 - Men's & Women's singles quarter-finals, Women's doubles semi-finals, Men's doubles quarter-finals, Wheelchair & Quad singles 1st round

Thursday, September 10 - Women's singles semi-finals, Men's doubles semi-finals, Wheelchair & Quad singles quarter-finals, Wheelchair & Quad doubles semi-finals

Saturday, September 12 - Women's singles final, Men's doubles final, Wheelchair singles

The day sessions begin at 4pm BST, while the evening sessions kick off at midnight.
