Previous winners of the US Open

Image: Novak Djokovic continues to chase tennis immortality

In the Open era, Roger Federer, Pete Sampras and Jimmy Connors are tied with the most men's singles titles, with five.

Novak Djokovic will be hoping to get to that number this year; he is tied on four with Rafael Nadal and John McEnroe as he continues to chase a record-breaking 25th Grand Slam title.

Serena Williams and Chris Evert share the record for women's titles with six, ahead of Steffi Graf (five) and Martina Navratilova (four).

Image: World No 1 Jannik Sinner won Wimbledon but has not played in Canada or Cincinnati

Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka are the respective reigning champions, though Emma Raducanu, Jannik Sinner, Iga Swiatek and Coco Gauff are also recent winners.

Sinner and Alcaraz will both show up to the US Open without having played in Canada or Cincinnati.

Since the beginning of the Masters format in 1990, no man has ever won the US Open without playing at least one of these two events.

US Open singles champions: Last 20 years Year Men's Women's 2005 Roger Federer Kim Clijsters 2006 Roger Federer Maria Sharapova 2007 Roger Federer Justine Henin 2008 Roger Federer Serena Williams 2009 Juan Martin del Potro Kim Clijsters 2010 Rafael Nadal Kim Clijsters 2011 Novak Djokovic Samantha Stosur 2012 Andy Murray Serena Williams 2013 Rafael Nadal Serena Williams 2014 Marin Cilic Serena Williams 2015 Novak Djokovic Flavia Penetta 2016 Stan Wawrinka Angelique Kerber 2017 Rafael Nadal Sloane Stephens 2018 Novak Djokovic Naomi Osaka 2019 Rafael Nadal Bianca Andreescu 2020 Dominic Thiem Naomi Osaka 2021 Daniil Medvedev Emma Raducanu 2022 Carlos Alcaraz Iga Swiatek 2023 Novak Djokovic Coco Gauff 2024 Jannik Sinner Aryna Sabalenka 2025 Carlos Alcaraz Aryna Sabalenka

Is Emma Raducanu playing?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look back at Emma Raducanu's incredible win at the 2021 US Open

No! The British No 1 will miss the Grand Slam because of the stress fracture in her right leg that she sustained during the grass-court season and forced her to pull out of Wimbledon.

It has been a frustrating 12 months for Raducanu with more persistent physical issues.

Will Jack Draper be forced to qualify for this year's tournament?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A drenched Jack Draper saw his 2024 US Open final dream disappear with the contents of his stomach as he lost in hot and humid conditions against Jannik Sinner

It looks that way! The 2024 semi-finalist missed out on a spot in the main draw after dropping outside of the top 128 in the world due to a recurrence of bone bruising in his left arm.

The injury has been a blow for the 24-year-old, who has managed only a handful of tournaments since first stepping away from the tour a year ago with the same issue.

Cameron Norrie and Britain's newest star Arthur Fery will feature at Flushing Meadows for the first time in his career after his remarkable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wild card which has seen his ranking soar.

A hat-trick for Sabalenka?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open final between Aryna Sabalenka and Amanda Anisimova

World No 1 Sabalenka will look to become the first woman to win three straight US Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14, while Sinner will be trying to regain the title that Alcaraz took from the 2024 champion when they met in last year's final.

The top-ranked Italian is coming off his fifth Grand Slam, after beating French Open winner Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final.

What about Serena Williams' return?

Image: Serena Williams could be the story of the US Open providing she is fit and healthy

Williams, 44, made her shock return to competition at Wimbledon, where she lost in three sets to Maya Joint before knee trouble forced her to pull out of doubles with her sister, Venus.

A wild card appearance at the Cincinnati Open alongside Venus could allow her to evaluate her knee before committing to the US Open where she would become arguably the biggest story of the tournament.

Sports.title: Root made 'grown up' call on curfew but does he have the feel for captaincy?
Sports.content:
Nasser Hussain hailed new England Test captain Joe Root's decision to abolish a team curfew but fears the returning skipper sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes.

Root has captained England on a record 65 occasions, most recently during their second Test defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended for breaking a team curfew that was introduced off the back of the 4-1 Ashes defeat in the winter.

To view this content you can use the button below to allow Captivate cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

"It's just a grown up decision, isn't it?" Hussain said on the latest Sky Sports Cricket Podcast of Root's decision to axe said curfew ahead of the three-Test series against Pakistan - live on Sky Sports - starting Wednesday.

"You've lost the team if you've got a curfew. You've got no control over your team.

"There's nothing good that happens with curfews because someone will end up breaking it.

"Just treat people like grown ups, and if they don't behave like grown ups, then the first thing you do is fine them, and then the second thing you do is leave them out.

"A professional sporting outfit shouldn't need a curfew, and it just shows how bad a place they were in that a curfew was put in.

"I'm really pleased that Joe has said 'no, enough of that nonsense'."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News correspondent Geraint Hughes provides background details on the appointments of Stephen Fleming as head coach and Joe Root as captain to the England Test set-up

The immediate task facing Root is to revive an England side that have lost eight of their last 13 Test matches following on from the 2-1 series loss to New Zealand that ended the 'Bazball' era and also saw the international retirement of Stokes.

Root's first permanent stint as skipper, however, also ended with a similarly barren run, with just one win in his final 17 Tests before he resigned from the captaincy in 2022.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking after the New Zealand Test win in 2022, Joe Root explained why he'd taken the decision to step away from Test captaincy

"He was given the biggest of hospital passes [for the second Test against New Zealand] at The Oval," Hussain said. "That was very recent, that wasn't four years ago, and it brought back some of the memories of Joe as a captain.

"For such a great player that has a feel for the tempo of a game, in that game at The Oval, he didn't have the feel of the game.

"He almost was trying to be a bit too Ben Stokes-ish, having men on the drive on a bouncy Oval pitch where balls were going behind.

"He doesn't quite have the feel of the game. And that's what I liked about Stokes' captaincy. He had a real feel for it.

"I'm pleased he's doing it, although I may have gone in the direction of Harry Brook, because I do see with Harry in white-ball cricket that he has a real feel for the game.

"He has an aura about him, but I understand the caveats of the schedule and all that sort of stuff."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England managing director Rob Key explains why it was 'the right thing to do' in giving Joe Root the Test captaincy over vice-captain Harry Brook

Athers: Root genuinely excited by captaincy return

Brook, despite being vice-captain, was overlooked to skipper the side for that second Test against New Zealand at The Oval.

Given his captaincy of the England white-ball sides, there may have been a reluctancy to overburden the 27-year-old with the permanent Test job, while his altercation with a nightclub bouncer the night before an ODI against New Zealand last winter drew heavy criticism.

"I put to Root, 'are you doing this out of duty or real desire?'" said Michael Atherton, who recently interviewed Root.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gives his first interview since being reappointed England Test captain

"Duty in the sense that there is really nobody else. Once they don't want Harry Brook to do it over three formats, where else do they go?

"But I sense he's genuinely very excited by the opportunity. He feels as though he's got some ammunition there in terms of his faster bowlers.

"And I thought he trod a nice line between being loyal to what has gone before. He continues to speak very highly about Brendon McCullum.

"I think he genuinely felt McCullum was a good coach for him as a batter and a good coach for the team, albeit it ended badly.

"He was careful not to say he's going to throw everything out. He wants to take the bits of Bazball that worked but perhaps put his own stamp on it.

"I thought the most important thing that he said was that he's not going to look to try and impose a predetermined style on this team."

Sports.title: Who's really in F1's title race and what factors will decide fight?
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli is the clear front-runner in Formula 1's 2026 title battle, but which drivers retain a realistic chance of catching him, and what will decide whether a comeback can be successful?

Mercedes driver Antonelli, who does not turn 20 until next week, exceeded all expectations to establish a 50-point lead at the top of the standings going into the summer break after the first 11 rounds.

The season resumes live on Sky Sports F1 this weekend with the Dutch Grand Prix, the first of 12 remaining scheduled races, and one of two remaining Sprint events.

Who could catch Antonelli?

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari - 2nd, 50 points behind Antonelli

The seven-time world champion is Antonelli's nearest challenger and is driving a Ferrari that has been the car most consistently capable of challenging Mercedes during the first half of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, David Croft questioned whether Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can challenge Antonelli for this season's world championship

A scrappy run of performances before the break saw the momentum Hamilton had built earlier in the summer fizzle out, but the 41-year-old will no doubt return refreshed and fully intent on rediscovering his best form in Zandvoort.

A strong start in Zandvoort is important for all the drivers chasing Antonelli, but perhaps especially for Hamilton and his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, who may well need to gain a significant upper hand within the team to have the support required to mount a sustained challenge.

Drivers' Championship - Top Five Driver Points 1) Kimi Antonelli 219 2) Lewis Hamilton 169 3) George Russell 160 4) Charles Leclerc 138 5) Lando Norris 128

George Russell, Mercedes - 3rd, 59 points behind Antonelli

If there was a driver who needed the summer break, it was Russell.

Luck, and then form, deserted the Brit over the first half of the season, but he still has what was undoubtedly the fastest car on the grid across the first 11 races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell and Antonelli react to their respective seventh and third-place finishes at the Hungarian Grand Prix

If a refreshed Russell, who had something to smile about over the summer break as he got engaged, can somehow rediscover his best form, he still has plenty of time to re-establish himself as a factor in the title battle.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari - 4th, 81 points behind Antonelli

After a tough run of races, Leclerc appeared to finally get to grips with the SF-26 over the final month before the break.

The Monegasque won at Silverstone and outscored Hamilton at the last three races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc won the British Grand Prix after the Safety Car was redeployed at the last moment for the final lap

However, his spring struggles have left next to no margin for error during the run-in, with the challenge of hauling in Hamilton a first hurdle for him to worry about before catching Antonelli.

Lando Norris, McLaren - 5th, 91 points behind Antonelli

The reigning world champion was very much out of this conversation until he produced an absolutely dominant victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix in the final race before the break.

The significant upgrade package McLaren brought to Hungary appeared to work very well, and Norris may well have won by half a minute if it were not for the fact he spent half the race stuck behind his team-mate Oscar Piastri after being overtaken on the first lap.

If McLaren's car works as well in Zandvoort as it did in Budapest, Norris cannot be discounted.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris reacts to his first win of 2026 saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

Which factors will be decisive?

Upgrades - With this being the first season of a new regulations cycle, there remains the possibility of major swings in performance as the teams continue to bring upgrades.

Although there are minor changes to the regulations for 2027, the teams can be expected to keep pushing hard in terms of development, as most of what they bring to their cars now is likely to provide useful knowledge - and potentially performance - next season.

After seeing McLaren leap forward in Hungary, Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur pointed out that his team's approach has been to bring regular upgrades rather than big packages like the one the Woking squad had in Hungary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Norris' victory last time out in Hungary, David Croft debates whether McLaren are now capable of winning further races or not

Although some of the summer break represents a shutdown where work is not allowed to be done, major upgrades are expected to arrive up and down the pit lane in Zandvoort and for the Italian Grand Prix a week later.

There is also the matter of engine upgrades. The FIA's Additional Development Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) system has already allowed Ferrari to bring an update to their power unit.

Another one could bring them closer to the performance of the field-leading Mercedes power unit, which it remains unclear whether they have been able to upgrade after it was initially, highly controversially, adjudged to be less strong than Red Bull's.

Reliability - While the Mercedes power unit has been the strongest, it has also had far more major issues than Ferrari's.

Both Mercedes and McLaren, who use their rival's power unit as a customer, have suffered multiple costly failures.

Despite having less grunt, Ferrari's power unit has proved highly reliable, which has been a key factor in keeping both the team and its drivers in the hunt for this year's titles.

Antonelli, who has suffered this season at the hands of a wheel-guard failure as well as an engine blowout, will be left vulnerable if he suffers any more DNFs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli suffered damage during the British Grand Prix

Penalties - The cost of poor reliability is not necessarily limited to the weekend it occurs on, with an irreparable power unit potentially leading to penalties later on in the season.

Each driver has a limit of four power units for the season, and both Antonelli and Russell are expected to need to exceed their allowance after losing an engine to reliability earlier in the season.

Top teams usually opt to take the penalty at a circuit where overtaking is relatively easy, allowing them to use the fresh power unit to surge back through the field and minimise the potential damage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell reacts to stopping on track during qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix due to a water leak

Driving (styles) - The radical change from last year's cars to this year's has required significant adjustment from the drivers.

Russell and Leclerc comfortably outperformed their team-mates last year but have been on the receiving end this season, while Piastri has recently appeared unable to match Norris.

While Leclerc seemed to make some positive adjustments, Russell was still trying to find a method that works in Hungary, and only finding a style that works for the Brit is going to give him a chance.

As for Antonelli, Hamilton and Norris, they all seem to be enjoying the way the nimbler 2026 cars handle.

It could be fascinating to watch three generations of drivers battle at the top of their games over the remaining races.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

Experience - While it will not help in terms of pure speed, experience could be a crucial factor coming down the stretch.

Four-time world champion Max Verstappen was able to apply huge pressure to Norris and Piastri, who were both seeking a maiden title, at the end of last year.

As Antonelli potentially gets closer to the finish line, the pressure on the Italian will ramp up.

It also remains to be seen whether Hamilton, whose last title came in 2020, could feel a similarly extreme level of pressure as he seeks a record eighth championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton explains why Ferrari are performing better this year compared to 2025

One would expect Hamilton to be comfortable in the heat of a title battle, while Norris also holds an edge over Russell and Leclerc having come through the fire 12 months ago.

While Antonelli does not have the experience himself, his team certainly does. His race engineer Peter 'Bono' Bonnington was in Hamilton's ear for six of the Brit's seven championships, and has already played a crucial role in guiding his young driver throughout the season so far.

Calendar - This element is very much out of the hands of the teams and drivers.

Ongoing conflict in the Middle East means doubt remains over whether the final two rounds of the season can go ahead as scheduled in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

The Bahrain Grand Prix, which was unable to take place in April, is going to be held in Malaysia in October, while the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix has been lost completely.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Formula 1 has added Malaysia to its 2026 schedule to host the Bahrain Grand Prix that was postponed earlier in the season

F1 president Stefano Domenicali says contingency plans are in place for the last two races to be held at alternative venues in Europe, with a deadline for a decision coming around the middle of September.

However, gossip in the paddock potentially points towards only one of the two season-ending races being replaced, with Italy's Imola circuit expected to step in.

All will be revealed on the front over the next month, but one less race would, at this stage, provide a major boost for Antonelli out front, and a blow to those chasing him.

Sports.title: Lingfield, Windsor and Wolverhampton feature on Monday
Sports.content:
Mithaaly faces Fairly Well and Nobelos in an interesting maiden contest at Windsor, live on Sky Sports Racing.

5.55 Windsor - Mithaaly bids to get off the mark

Mithaaly bids to get his head in front for the first time under Billy Loughnane in the Play The Matchbook Match 6 Maiden Stakes.

The George Boughey-trained 260,000gns purchase is yet to win from two starts, yet he has shaped with promise on both occasions. He finished half a length behind Rocket Boy at Yarmouth the last day, who subsequently ran a stormer when placing third in the Stonehenge Stakes at Salisbury.

From the raced horses, Fairy Well clearly sets the standard with two solid efforts in the form book. Notably at Leicester she finished behind Coat Of Red, who went on to frank the form when going close behind smart two-year-olds Evenfall and Sorrengail at Newbury.

Nobelos should provide the stiffest opposition of the newcomers, having been purchased for €110,000 at the Goffs Orby Sale, and any market clues may prove informative.

6.55 Windsor - Unexposed Ray Mon Dough headlines handicap

Ray Mon Dough looked potentially very smart when bolting up on debut at two last November and, still unexposed, he goes for gold in tonight's Matchbook Loves Racing Handicap.

He has taken a bit of time to come to hand this season but showed promise when second to exciting prospect (and now Listed winner) Behike. After not finding Chester to his liking in July, he truly showed his quality when winning with plenty in hand with a refitted tongue strap at Leicester. He should remain ahead of the handicapper today.

Waistcoat won impressively at Newbury last month and, although up in class, he can run creditably. Under The Twilight and Cashbox arguably bring stronger pieces of form to the table, with both finishing in the places at Glorious Goodwood.

Amazonian Dream found it too competitive at the end of July, but this course specialist cannot be counted out down in grade for the Rod Millman team.

8.10 Wolverhampton - James Choice and Prince Of Calypso renew rivalry

The progressive duo of James Choice and Prince Of Calypso renew their rivalry in the Follow @attheraces On Instagram Handicap.

Prince Of Calypso put his Thirsk blip behind him to continue his progressive trajectory when sticking to the task well and finishing third in a 14-runner handicap at Southwell last month.

In the same race, James Choice was the bigger eye-catcher, with the highest finishing speed of 111.87% to edge out the former on the line. This bodes well with an extra furlong sure to suit, as they put nearly four lengths into the fourth, and only went down to the progressive Sir Mark Prescott stayer Roc De Fer.

Clansman could prove competitive markedly down in grade, although this is definitely the shortest he needs nowadays.

Optician and Joseph are relatively consistent and should run solid races to round off this well contested affair.

Elsewhere...

Magical Life looks to back up an impressive six-length victory at Kempton last time when she lines up for the opening Free Bets On attheraces.com Nursery Handicap at Lingfield. William Cox's mount was raised 6lbs for that victory by the handicapper and it remains to be seen whether this Territories filly can handle the hike in the weights.

On the continent, Clairefontaine plays host to the Listed Prix Des Enfoires at 5.30pm. Former British-based rider Bryony Le Clerc (Frost) rides Inner Success in this one.

Sports.title: ‘That’s the standard’: Mikel Arteta hails Arsenal’s desire on blue day for Maresca
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players demonstrated their hunger to defend the Premier League title in their Community Shield triumph over Manchester City. Arsenal, who ended their 22-year wait last season and are seeking to win back-to-back top-flight titles for the first time since 1934-35, beat City 3-0 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff in Enzo Maresca’s first significant match in charge.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after 24 seconds, the fastest goal in the competition since Bobby Owen’s strike for City in 1968, before Kai Havertz doubled Arsenal’s lead and their captain, Martin Ødegaard, completed the scoring on 48 minutes. The 3-0 defeat represented the joint-heaviest loss for a City manager in their first game in charge, with Harry Newbould the most recent to suffer a three-goal opening defeat – 4-1, also to Arsenal, in 1906. It is also Maresca’s joint-heaviest defeat as a manager in England.

Arteta was delighted with Arsenal’s convincing display. “I am obviously extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” he said. “We talked about the desire we have to start the season and to show ourselves how much we want it and I saw a lot of positive things against a top opponent. I’m very impressed in the manner that we played, in the manner that we competed. That’s the standard for us. If we drive the standards at this level, I’m sure that we’re going to be really, really competitive.”

Asked about the desire displayed by his team, he said: “Because we want to go straight again. The desire comes [because] I want to live that moment again. I want to live other moments, even bigger than them … we know what it’s going to take. We know the difficulty of the task. We’ve never done it at this club, to win it again. We know that it’s going to demand something special and we are ready for it.”

Arteta praised the performance of Christos Tzolis, who was involved in all three goals. “He is a really intelligent boy and he has a massive quality, which is when he is in the last 20-30m [of the pitch] he is so composed to pick people out in and around the box,” said the Arsenal manager. “And also to finish actions and he has shown that again two or three times. He was decisive.”

View image in fullscreen New signing Christos Tzolis was involved in all three of Arsenal’s goals. Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA

Ødegaard said the team’s performance was evidence they are capable of winning back-to-back titles. “We played some brilliant football,” said Arsenal’s captain. “[It was a] great performance and a great way to start the season. I always want to help the team as much as possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals. We showed our level today. We’ve shown we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again. We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again. We want to win everything.”

Maresca acknowledged City, who are closing on a deal to sign Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi as they prepare to sell Rodri to Barcelona, would welcome new arrivals before their league opener at home to Bournemouth on Sunday. Rodri did not travel to Cardiff, where Elliot Anderson started in midfield, and Jack Grealish arrived from the substitutes’ bench for his first City appearance since May 2025. “Any new signing, the sooner they arrive the better because we are starting the Premier League in one week and if they start to work with us as soon as possible it’s better that they can also understand the way we want to play,” he said.

Maresca said he was not alarmed by the manner of the defeat. “In general I’m always concerned, even when we win games so imagine how [concerned] that we didn’t win the game,” said the Italian, who succeeded Pep Guardiola this summer. “It’s just the beginning, we have many things that we need to do better, I think the reaction was good after conceding the first goal and now try to reset and analyse the game and think from Tuesday about the next game.”

Sports.title: Rodri set to complete Barcelona move after Manchester City accept £65.4m bid
Sports.content:
Rodri looks set to complete a move to Barcelona after Manchester City accepted a bid of £65.4m from the Spanish club.

The 30-year-old World Cup winner had entered the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium and made it clear he would like the opportunity to move to Barcelona. City, who are now closing in on a deal to sign Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, were reluctant sellers but had little choice with the Spanish international out of contract next summer.

City had already rejected Barcelona’s bid of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri last week after an initial offer of €45m (£38.5m) but have now accepted the latest bid.

Speaking after City’s 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, Enzo Maresca called Rodri a “top player” and said “all the teams need Rodri”, but City have been unable to persuade their linchpin to stay and sign a new contract. Rodri had only returned to the club on Friday, having undergone back surgery after the World Cup, with Maresca saying he had given him a “big hug” when he first met up with him.

Rodri has spent seven seasons with City, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the only goal when they beat Inter in the 2023 Champions League final. The following year he won the Ballon d’Or but, by the time he was presented with the trophy, he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament which ruled him out of most of the 2024-25 campaign, while hamstring and groin problems limited him to 33 appearances in Pep Guardiola’s final campaign in charge.

City have already undergone major changes in midfield this summer, spending £116m on Elliot Anderson, while agreeing a deal to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah. They are now ready to seal a move for the Morocco star Bouaddi.

The teenager impressed at the World Cup and Lille had initially wanted any potential move to include a 12-month loan deal back to the French side. However, with City losing Bernardo Silva and now Rodri, Maresca is keen to bulk up his midfield options for the new campaign and want Bouaddi available for this season. City have also been linked with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández and retain an interest.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 11: Hull City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 20th (NB: this is not necessarily Louise Taylor’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th (Championship)

Prospects

It is no exaggeration to say that Hull’s playoff triumph in May was a shock. They had, after all, started the season as Championship relegation favourites and operated under a transfer embargo throughout the campaign. Moreover, they conceded 66 league goals, the fourth-highest, along the way. Now another minor miracle will surely be required if Premier League survival is to be secured.

Much may hinge on Oli McBurnie, the scorer of 19 goals last season, succeeding where he has struggled in the past and retaining his scoring touch in the top tier, but there is no lack of optimism in East Yorkshire. “Think about us like a volcano,” says Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.”

Hull intend following Sunderland’s template last summer by making 14 new signings, albeit on a significantly smaller budget. So far 11 – Jack Butland, Hidemasa Morita, Matt Targett, Óscar Zambrano, Jens Hjertø-Dahl, Elliot Stroud, Konstantinos Tzolakis, Lucas Herrington, Joe Gelhardt, Lucas Gourna-Douath and the club record buy, the central defender Nobel Mendy, who has arrived from Rayo Vallecano for just over £20m – have arrived.

“The transfer market is very slow,” said the manager, Sergej Jakirovic, who covets the Sunderland striker Wilson Isidor and last season’s 23-goal Championship top scorer, Swansea’s Zan Vipotnik. “But, in the last seven days of the window, it will become very, very quick.”

His cause has been hindered by pre-season injuries, with perhaps the biggest blow involving an arm problem suffered by Butland. It threatens to keep the former Rangers goalkeeper, who had impressed in friendlies, out until Christmas. The consensus is that Hull will have long since become a lost cause by then, but, much as the impressive Jakirovic needs new faces and Premier League nous, he does hold one ace card. Hull boast an exceptionally powerful team spirit driven by exemplary on-field leaders, including the veteran central defender John Egan. Maybe, just maybe, it can, once again, transport them further than anyone believes possible.

Off-field picture

In June, the playoff winners faced kicking off the new Premier League season handicapped by a near certain six-point deduction. A club that spent last season under a two-window English Football League transfer embargo avoided it by selling their goalkeeper Ivor Pandur and midfielder Aidon Shehu to Rangers and Panathinaikos respectively for a combined £8.5m. Access to the fruits of the top tier’s broadcast deal has since made Hull a whole lot wealthier, but Ilicali has pledged not to risk the club’s future by overspending and, at the time of writing, has invested around £78m on the new players.

Owner-fan relationship

Unpredictable and slightly conflicted. Ilicali, the Turkish sports reporter turned media mogul – who is on his fifth manager since taking control in early 2022 – was offered a wholesale welcome when he took over from the unpopular Allam family, but he now exerts much more of a polarising effect on supporters. If November 2022, when he treated 320 fans to an all-expenses-paid week’s holiday at a luxury resort hotel in Antalya represented a high point, a nadir arrived when late payments resulted in Hull being placed under a transfer embargo last season. Nonetheless, the playoff triumph ensures many are prepared to offer the 57-year-old the benefit of the doubt.

The manager

The Mostar-born, 49-year-old Jakirovic has Bosnian and Croatian citizenship and says his life was shaped by the 1990s Balkan war that broke out when he was 14. “It was life or death,” he has said. “It has made me the person I am today.” Shortly after his arrival from Turkey’s Kayserispor, in June 2025, Hull were placed under a transfer embargo, but, defying widespread predictions of imminent relegation, he led the team to sixth place before beating Middlesbrough in the Championship playoff final. A central midfielder or central defender in his playing days, the former Bosnia and Herzegovina international led Dinamo Zagreb to the Croatian League and Cup double in 2024.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Hidemasa Morita applauds the Sporting fans during the Portuguese Cup final in May, his last appearance for the Lisbon club. Photograph: SPP Sport Press Photo/Alamy

The Japan defensive midfielder Hidemasa Morita joined from Sporting Lisbon after four trophy-laden years in Portugal. A fans’ favourite in Lisbon, he played regular Champions League football last season as Sporting reached the quarter-finals and has 40 senior international caps. Morita could have stayed in Lisbon, but opted not to renew his contract in order to experience Premier League football. Hull fended off competition from Ipswich for the signature of the 31-year-old who was a key part of the Japan squad at Qatar 2022. Morita is the second Japanese player to represent Hull and his amalgam of experience and quality in a key position promise to prove invaluable.

Stat attack

The strangest part of the Championship playoffs might not have been the Southampton spying scandal. Hull were second-bottom for expected points, 53.1, and would have been relegated if underlying performances determined results. It was remarkable tthey won promotion and it will be even more surprising if they make a serious fist of staying up.

Set for a breakthrough

The 22-year-old central defender Charlie Hughes was Hull’s young player of the year last season and his assurance in possession and excellent passing range are bound to catch all sorts of Premier League eyes. Helpfully, his ballplaying ability is matched by some equally impressive – and combative – defending. After spending his youth in the academies of Liverpool and Manchester City, Hughes joined Wigan, leaving for Hull last summer. An imposing blend of steel and silk, a defender also comfortable in central midfield will miss the start of the season after hernia surgery. Happily, Hughes is expected back by early autumn at the latest and appears integral to the team’s survival hopes.

World Cup impact

Not content with helping Hull win the most unexpected of promotions, the Canada winger Liam Millar headed across the Atlantic to the World Cup. He made three appearances at the tournament as they reached the knockout stage, losing to Morocco in the round of 16. Given his career seemed in real jeopardy when he suffered a serious knee injury shortly after joining Hull in 2024, inclusion in Canada’s squad represented the fulfilment of an unlikely looking dream. “It was an unbelievable experience,” said the 26-year-old. “I’ve never seen Canada the way it was, I’ve never seen so many red shirts in Vancouver and Toronto. We want to inspire the next generation and I think we did Canada proud.”

Sports.title: Flemming’s dramatic Burnley double pegs back West Ham on Championship return
Sports.content:
There are many good reasons why Burnley and West Ham are performing as Premier League tribute acts, slumming it in the Championship with the hope of a shot at the limelight once more. They are two flawed teams, relegated because of chronic defects, and plenty were on show as West Ham blew a two-goal lead to start life on the second-tier circuit with an entertaining draw.

Zian Flemming’s late double secured a thoroughly deserved point for the hosts, who showed promise going forward but took far too long to find a clinical finish. Despite going two goals ahead through Maximilian Kilman and Manor Solomon, West Ham rarely looked comfortable as they sat back, something that eventually cost them.

“We did a very good first half,” Nuno Espírito Santo said. “We created a lot of situations we were able to control and stop Burnley. Not so good in the second half, but after we scored the second goal, I think we should have done better to keep the result.”

Nuno continued his career-long love of conservatism and his side were put under pressure early on, only surviving through Burnley’s poor decision-making and inept finishing. In addition to continuity in the dugout, West Ham can boast their captain, Jarrod Bowen, who committed to the club rather than seek a quick return to the top flight this summer. It was his corner that found Kilman at the back post after he lost Aaron Ramsey in the box.

Considering West Ham are favourites to go back up, this fortuitous lead should have been a foundation to build on, but little attempt was made to seek a second. They were passive for long periods, composed in possession, but Burnley were able to counter at speed through the midfield and cause problems, only to lack the composure to make the most of those situations.

Nuno tried to rectify the faltering midfield by sending on James Ward-Prowse for the anonymous Pablo, a player who has yet to find his level in England. It made no difference as Burnley came out the better side, pinning West Ham back repeatedly, but Flemming appeared destined to not score, finding the fans, goalkeeper, the inside of the post and Ollie Scarles on the line rather than the back of the net.

West Ham reminded everyone that they possess Premier League quality as Mohamadou Kanté made light work of Marcus Edwards on the right wing before pulling the ball back to Solomon to slam home from close range. This was their second and final shot on target, both leading to goals. Despite being second best, the visitors must have believed they were out of sight, by accident rather than design.

View image in fullscreen Maximilian Kilman gives West Ham the lead as he heads home Jarrod Bowen’s cross. Photograph: COLORSPORT/Alan Martin/Shutterstock

Flemming had other ideas as things finally clicked, aided by Scarles crudely taking out Edwards in the box, allowing the striker to settle his nerves after 83 minutes of near misses and create tension in the West Ham ranks. It worked as the visitors failed to clear a corner which Flemming swept home in the second minute of added time, further explaining why he has attracted transfer interest. Asked if Flemming will stay the Burnley manager, Nicky Hayen, who is desperate not to lose his talisman, said: “It does not help that he scored twice today.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Nuno will want more action in the transfer market after the record Championship signing of Arne Engels from Celtic on Saturday. A striker is much needed as Taty Castellanos made little impact, while the aforementioned Pablo does not give the impression of a man who will fire West Ham to promotion. The bench featured five academy graduates, none of who Nuno felt comfortable bringing on, which says a lot. “The club knows the targets and the needs of the team. [We are] working very hard and trying to get the bodies in as soon as possible,” Nuno said. “We need especially in the offensive part of the team.”

Hayen, celebrating his 46th birthday, took his team on a lap of honour after his first league game in charge as he aims to build a relationship with supporters, who suffered through plenty of unwatchable football under his predecessor. “We showed resilience and that’s why I’m really satisfied for these boys because they worked really hard to change this game around and also how we did it,” Hayen said. “I’m pleased with the fans, how they supported us for 95 minutes. We invested a lot of time before this game into them because what we wanted was really to find the connection with them, that we made the promise that we bring energy into the stadium, that we keep on going for 95 minutes and this is exactly what we did.”

Sports.title: Brighton’s Emilie Joramo: ‘I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be’
Sports.content:
Emilie Joramo has long had her sights set on the Women’s Super League, but she held herself back from pushing for a move over from Scandinavia – until now.

“I’d been interested in the league for a long time now and it was a goal for me to get here one day,” says Joramo, who Brighton signed on a free transfer at the end of June. “It was about finding the right path for me to get here. I didn’t want to go too early, I wanted to feel ready for it both physically and mentally. Now, everything just felt right.”

Brighton had been tracking the Norwegian midfielder for some time and the 24-year-old was aware of their interest. An encouraging conversation with Brighton’s manager, Dario Vidosic, and good meetings with the club as her contract with Hammarby drew closer to its end meant she was at last ready to join the league she had followed from afar.

That time in Sweden with Hammarby, with whom she reached the Europa Cup final last season, and before that in her homeland with Rosenborg who she helped win the Norwegian Cup for the first time in 21 years, was crucial in preparing her for her latest challenge.

“I had so much fun at Hammarby and I’ve got so many good friends there,” she says. “I grew both as a football player and as a person in those years. I didn’t feel ready when I was 21, when I went to Sweden, to come over here. I felt like I needed to play a bit more, to play every game, that was really important for me.”

That Brighton had been aware of her for some time was a boost too. “It’s reassuring for me that they really wanted me,” she says. “They hadn’t just watched a couple games, they’d been following me for years, and that’s really important to me because I’m not going to jump at the first opportunity I get. I like to think things through and it has to feel right for me.”

View image in fullscreen Emilie Joramo played Champions League qualifying last year, and helped Hammarby reach the final of the inaugural Europa Cup Photograph: Emma Wallskog/Bildbyrån/Shutterstock

For Brighton fans wondering what they are getting, there should be some excitement too. Joramo is fiercely motivated and feels she fits the possession-based style of football that Vidosic wants his team to play.

“I would say that I’m a hardworking player,” she says, when asked to describe herself. “I always give 100% all of the time. I can’t do 50, 60, 70, I’m always 100%. I want to have the ball. I want to play, not just put balls in behind but to keep the ball , play with each other, [build] good relationships with the other players and think several steps ahead. They’ve always been things that I’m good at and I’m always wanting to get better at too.”

Brighton and the WSL present a step up. “I think I can get challenged a lot here because things go much faster, the intensity is higher, you have a smaller amount of time when you have the ball,” she says. “So, it’s a perfect place for me to be at now to be challenged further and develop my strengths but also the parts that I’m not as strong at and need to develop more.”

Arriving and starting life on the south coast was “a bit overwhelming” in the beginning: “There’s so many people to get to know, the staff is so much bigger than what I’ve been used to. So, instead of one physio you have five and you need to get to know everyone and get to know which person does which role. That’s always the way it is in a new team, of course, but it’s much bigger here.”

Everyone has been very welcoming and her first impressions of training sessions under Vidosic have been positive. “I’ve only had two sessions with him so far,” she says, “but he seems very, very good at football tactics, how the game works, how to play good football, and that was important for me because I’m a player that wants to have the ball and always wants to try to get better and try to play good football together as a team, not only as individuals. This is what Dario wants, so it really fits my ambitions, my values and how I want to play.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Emilie Joramo was Brighton’s second signing of the summer window – they have since added five more. Photograph: James Boardman/Brighton and Hove Albion

She is finding her feet on the pitch, and starting to find them off it. Joramo’s girlfriend has moved to England with her, which has helped the transition and helps her escape football when needed. “I have to have other things to do besides football,” she says. “We’ve been to the beach and have been exploring the city. It’s so different for me to live by the beach, I’m from the mountains and the woods. This is like a holiday for me, and with the weather as well, it’s been so warm. It’s really nice.”

The goal now is “to contribute as much as I can to this team and play as much as I can”, but Joramo’s patience as she worked towards her WSL goal should continue to serve her well. “I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be and develop in and I need to give it a bit of time in the beginning, because I can be very impatient,” she says. “I have to give it some time to get into it, get into the intensity and everything around the game here, because it’s so much more than what I’m used to in Sweden, this is so much bigger.”

At the end of her first season in England is a big carrot, should Norway come through a two-legged playoff against Romania and then another against Albania or Wales and qualify for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

Joramo made her debut for the senior side in 2022 and has been on the fringes of the squad since, making three appearances in total and playing for the under-23s. In April she was on the bench for the senior side’s back-to-back qualification campaign wins over Slovenia and she is hopeful her WSL move helps her show what she can bring.

“Hopefully this also will strengthen my opportunities with the national team,” she says. “I know this is the best league in the world, so if I get to play here, then I’ve done something right, I think.”

Sports.title: Scotland appoint Pocognoli as successor to Clarke in fresh approach
Sports.content:
The Scottish Football Association has appointed the Belgian Sébastien Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke as manager. The 39-year-old, who was sacked by Monaco in June, will become the country’s first non-Scottish manager since Berti Vogts, who was in charge from 2002 to 2004.

Clarke’s abrupt departure came after Scotland were knocked out of the World Cup at the group stage. He had signed a four-year contract extension immediately before the tournament. It quickly became clear the SFA would turn towards a foreign manager with the Danes Jon Dahl Tomasson and Kasper Hjulmand being linked with the position.

Pocognoli, a left-back who played for Brighton and West Brom, will probably be welcomed by Scotland fans seeking a fresh approach. Clarke was in position for a generally successful seven years, including appearances at three major tournaments, but was often criticised for a pragmatic style.

Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief football officer, said Pocognoli “will bring an aggressive, front-foot style of play that will excite supporters”.

After a period in youth coaching, Pocognoli enjoyed a successful time in charge of Union Saint-Gilloise in his homeland. Under Pocognoli, Union won their first title in 90 years in 2025. A move to Monaco followed, but Pocognoli lasted eight months and 38 games in France. The former Everton and Belgum winger Kevin Mirallas is expected to join him in the dugout.

Pocognoli said: “When I first heard of the interest, I was immediately excited about the opportunity. Scotland’s supporters are famous for their passion – most recently at the World Cup in the USA - and I have experienced it myself as a player for Belgium when we played in 2013.

“Along with my coaching staff, I will do everything I can to give them a team to be proud of and build on the success that has been achieved already by my predecessor.”
