Scotland begin their Nations League campaign with a trip to Slovenia on 26 September. Pocognoli’s first home game in charge will be Switzerland’s visit to Glasgow three days later.

Sports.title: Nabizada stunner edges Watford past Southampton as ‘Spygate’ still looms large
Sports.content:
Southampton will have to get used to being barracked as they travel the Championship this autumn, the “Spygate” team set to be everyone’s favourite boo boys in the second tier. Certainly that was the case in Hertfordshire, with Watford fans and players alike beside themselves after a hard-fought victory, decided by two memorable first-half goals.

Tonda Eckert, the Southampton head coach, remains under investigation for his part in the Spygate affair and presented a subdued figure both during and after this contest. He insisted that his team were more united than ever after suffering the indignity of being removed from last season’s playoffs, “but it would be easier to say that after a victory”, Eckert acknowledged.

Watford paid tribute to Kenny Jackett before the match, the one-club legend and local boy hailed with two minutes of applause. This celebration of longevity and connection, with a Panini-inspired tifo tumbling down the stands, cut a contrast with the current operation, where Alessio Dionisi has become Watford’s 12th full-time manager in just the past five years.

“I am very tired and my team was too by the end,” said the Italian who was coaching Empoli in Serie B last season. Dionisi praised the attitude of his team – “I liked the mentality of my players, in every moment I saw one team working together,” he said. He also benefited from the Pozzo family’s multi-club network and the local academy in digging out a victory.

The Spain under-21 attacker Iker Bravo was one of several signings to make the familiar trek from “sister” club Udinese this summer, and he made his mark quickly, opening the scoring with a quite stunning solo goal in the 12th minute. It was all his own work and Bravo had to deploy a combination of skills to turn an innocuous situation into real danger. Looking to latch on to a long ball some 40 yards from goal, the 6ftplaymaker won the first header then, crucially, got a second touch with an outstretched toe to get the ball under control. Bravo then span immediately and drove at goal, pushing his way into the box before chopping right and getting off a low shot that Daniel Peretz got a hand to, butcould not keep out.

View image in fullscreen Watford’s Amin Nabizada jumps for joy after scoring their second goal against Southampton. Photograph: Peter Tarry/PA

A great way to start any season, the energy among the Vicarage Road crowd grew immediately and the home side went on to dominate the first half. They doubled their lead in the 29th minute with a moment to remember for 19-year-old academy graduate Amin Nabizada who exploited the same gaps on the left of the Southampton defence to run with the ball from his own half before finishing precisely from a tight angle. “Nabizada was emotional but after the first 10 minutes he played well,” Dionisi said. “When there is one mentality amongst the team, then it’s better for him too.”

Southampton had the better of the second half, taking advantage of a drop in tempo from the hosts to assert their interests. A spell of concerted possession in the 56th minute ended with Kuryu Matsuki pulling out wide, the young midfielder Cam Bragg moving unmarked into the half space and his shift left finding the Canada World Cup star Cyle Larin to poke home from 10 yards out.

Larin had a chance to equalise just two minutes later with a shot on the turn but Federico Ravaglia – another new signing to impress for the Hornets – turned the ball round the post. When Finn Azaz came on as a second-half substitute for the Saints he bought an inch to fire off a low drive that went just beyond the left hand post. As a succession of dangerous set pieces were sent over by Ryan Manning, Southampton fans were singing “we’ll score when we want”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But as the game passed through a flurry of substitutions Eckert’s team were unable to generate enough momentum to truly unsettle Dionisi’s men. Their only further chance came in added time and was scuffed wide by Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

Eckert said he had been happy enough with his team’s performance beyond “two errors in possession”. He insisted his squad are “very close and united” as a group. “We had a different expectation for the result but the group looks united and we now need to turn that into results.”

Opening matches rarely offer much insight into how a season will pan out. But Watford fans were able to enjoy both temperate weather and a decent performance. If Southampton want to transform the negative energy of Spygate into something positive, meanwhile, they will have to start again next week.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo says this year is ‘probably’ his last as a footballer
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo believes this year is “probably” his last as a professional footballer, the 41-year-old Portugal captain said in an interview with Vogue magazine published on Sunday.

Ronaldo, who has established his place among football’s all-time greats with more than 950 goals for club and country, had previously spoken of retiring “soon” or within “one or two years”.

“This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” the Al-Nassr forward told Vogue, saying his future after football was “all mapped out”.

“I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard,” he said, listing travel and padel among his favourite activities. “Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one.”

Ronaldo married his partner, Georgina Rodríguez, in an intimate ceremony in the Portuguese resort of Cascais on Tuesday. The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus player told Vogue he wanted to “continue to enjoy what I’ve earned – what we’ve earned. Because after all it’s been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice.”

After being part of the Portugal side which reached the last 16 of the World Cup this summer, Ronaldo is due to link up with Al-Nassr for the new Saudi Pro League season.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon praised by Barcelona fans as England winger enjoys 'electric' first friendly appearance since £70m deal to replace Marcus Rashford
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon was lauded as the 'best player on the pitch' as the England winger made his first appearance for Barcelona since completing a £70m transfer.

Barcelona had moved quickly at the end of last season to sign Gordon from Newcastle, with the surprise move completed at the end of May ahead of the World Cup.

The Spanish giants have been forced to wait to see Gordon feature following England's run to the World Cup semi-finals, with his post-tournament break leading to the 25-year-old starting his pre-season late.

Gordon, however, was quick to make an impression as he featured for the first time in a friendly against Barcelona.

In the opening minutes, Gordon showed his pace as he dribbled past his marker at speed, before firing in a dangerous low cross that neither Eric Garcia nor Raphinha were able to finish.

Operating on the left of Barcelona's attack, Gordon made several darting dribbles and looked to provide crosses from the byline.

Anthony Gordon made his first appearance in a Barcelona shirt in their friendly against Basel

The £70m summer signing from Newcastle caught the eye during the first half of the match

Gordon's eye-catching start was nearly capped with a solo goal, with the winger picking the ball up midway through the Basel half and driving goalwards.

The England star forced a slip from the defending full back, before cutting onto his right foot and firing narrowly over the bar.

Barcelona based newspaper Sport declared Gordon had been the Catalans’ ‘best player in attack’ after his ‘very, very active’ appearance.

Another journalist summarised: 'Great minutes from Gordon in the friendly match between Barça and Basel.

'The Englishman is increasingly shaking off his marker and has delivered some fine crosses into the box.'

Gordon ultimately only featured in the first half for Barcelona as he works his way back to full fitness in pre-season.

AS reported that Gordon has already convinced Barcelona boss Hansi Flick to give him a starting role despite having only been in training for the past week.

Barcelona fans, however, appeared impressed with Gordon's performance and were optimistic about his role ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Fellow new signing Karim Adeyemi was on target in Barcelona's 5-2 victory over Basel

'Gordon is such a breath of fresh air. He looks so electric and who needed zero adaption. Looking forward to him,' one said.

'Barcelona finally has a left winger that takes on defenders one on one Anthony Gordon. What a diamond,' another said.

A third wrote: 'Gordon will provide something that Barca has been lacking in recent seasons, a threat on the outside on the left. Also allows us to push the left sided midfielder higher and between the lines.'

LaLiga champions Barcelona had moved for Gordon at the start of the summer, with the club opting against signing fellow England international Marcus Rashford permanently after his loan spell last season.

Gordon had already impressed fans by speaking fluent Spanish at his unveiling, having revealed it had been a childhood dream to play for the Catalan side.

Barcelona earned a 5-2 victory in the friendly with fellow new signing Karim Adeyemi having opened the scoring in the first half.

Hamza Abdelkarim, Lamine Yamal and a brace from Jesse Bisiwu sealed Barcelona's victory.

Sports.title: Actress Hayden Panettiere dead at 36: Hollywood star known for roles in Heroes and Nashville remembered for bringing 'joy to all who knew her' after shock passing
Sports.content:
Actress Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36.

Panettiere, known for her roles on the hit NBC series Heroes and musical drama Nashville, was remembered as 'an incredible light and a force of nature.' She leaves behind an 11-year-old daughter.

Representatives for the former child star announced on Sunday: 'It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden.

'She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her - and to the millions who watched her onscreen.'

Her cause of death was not immediately clear.

But law enforcement sources confirmed to TMZ that police responded to an incident involving the actress and that an investigation is ongoing.

'There's an investigation ongoing,' her representative added in a statement to NBC News. 'We should know more tomorrow.'

Sources also told TMZ that Panettiere had been recently complaining of back pain and that she and her on-again, off-again boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, flew from Los Angeles to the south just one day before her tragic passing.

Beloved actress Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36. She leaves behind her daughter, who is 11. Panettiere is pictured here attending the Met Gala in 2014

Panettiere is seen on May 19, 2026 in New York City, promoting her new book. The tragic news comes just months after her memoir, This is Me, became a New York Times bestseller. The actress had become candid about her struggles dealing with fame, especially as a child star, in the months before her passing

Panettiere started out as a child star, with her first acting gig at just 11 months old

The Hollywood star earned multiple award nominations across her career, most notably while playing cheerleader Claire Bennet on Heroes and Juliette Barnes on Nashville.

Panettiere, who was set to turn 37 on Friday, also appeared in the Scream franchise as Kirby Reed, and lent her voice to the video games Until Dawn and Kingdom Hearts.

Panettiere is predeceased by her brother, Jensen, who passed away in February 2023 from 'an enlarged heart' at the age of 28.

Panettiere recently released a memoir

She said that she felt like she 'lost half of her soul' following his death, and revealed that the stress of his loss resulted in her body 'ballooning out', which left her in a 'really bad' and 'destructive' place.

The tragic news of her death comes just months after her memoir, This is Me: A Reckoning, became a New York Times bestseller.

In the book, Panettiere described how she contended with fame and handled the difficulties in her life.

She had suffered from drug addiction, beginning when she was just 15 years old.

At the time, she claimed she started taking 'happy pills' in an effort to make her seem more 'peppy' during interviews.

Her addiction then became worse while she was battling postpartum depression following the birth of her daughter Kaya in 2014.

But Panettiere has been sober in recent years, she said in a 2022 interview, noting that 'it's an everyday battle.'

Hayden Panettiere is pictured playing the character Claire Bennet in the NBC sci-fi drama series Heroes

The actress's younger brother, Jansen Panettiere, passed away in February 2023 from 'an enlarged heart'. They are seen together here in 2011

Hayden Panettiere has tragically died at the age of 36. Her cause of death was not immediately clear. The Hollywood star is pictured here at a gala in Hollywood in 2022

Panettiere leaves behind an 11-year-old daughter with ex, Wladimir Klitschko

'It's an everyday choice, and I'm checking in with myself all the time,' Panettiere told People at the time.

'But I'm just so grateful to be part of this world again, and I will never take it for granted again.'

Panettiere has also told how she nearly died during childbirth, and later relinquished custody of her daughter to her ex, former heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, while struggling with postpartum depression in 2018.

Her daughter now lives in Europe.

Speaking of the decision, Panettiere said she 'desperately' needed help at the time and insisted that Kaya does not feel 'abandoned' while appearing in a recent episode of the On Purpose with Jay Shetty podcast.

'The idea that anybody would think that I would just give away my child and be okay with it is heartbreaking. Couldn't be further from the truth,' Panettiere said.

'I was struggling with mental health and anxiety and postpartum and having to act my way through it, and just feeling like I completely lost myself,' she added.

Panettiere is remembered for her role as Claire Bennet on the hit NBC series Heroes

Panettiere is seen during her book tour in New York City in May

Panettiere is seen crying following her brother's celebration of life event in their hometown of Palisades, New York

Panettiere is pictured with her daughter, after telling how she almost died during childbirth

Panettiere has also come out as bisexual while she promoted her new book.

'It's sad that I had to wait till I was 36 years old to share that part of me, but better late than never, right?' the Nashville alum told Us Weekly in May.

'I've chosen to share it with the world, I'm comfortable saying I'm bisexual. I'm comfortable to confidently say that, yes, I am bisexual. I said it!'

Despite having little privacy due to 'paparazzi always outside waiting for me,' Panettiere still managed to secretly date women, whom she preferred to men from 'a very, very young age.'

'[I was] much more into women,' the two-time Golden Globe nominee said.

'But, yeah, I have explored it, but I don't think I ever had the courage, because I hadn't shared this with anybody.

'I didn't really have the courage to throw myself fully, emotionally into it, because then if I did fall in love, that wasn't something that I wanted to ever have to hide. I didn't feel confident enough, and I was too afraid to really let that part of me explore that part of me.'

By the age of 19, Panettiere dissolved her business relationship with her mother, who was also her manager at the time.

Panettiere came out as bisexual as she promoted her new book. The actress is pictured here as Claire Bennet in Heroes

She played Juliette Barnes on the ABC show Nashville, releasing a number of her own songs

Panettiere is pictured with actor Adrian Pasdar on the set of Heroes

Panettiere was born on August 21, 1989 in Palisades, New York.

She first started acting at just 11 months old, appearing in a commercial.

Her full-time acting career then began in 1994 when she played Sarah Roberts in the ABC soap opera One Life to Live until 1997. She then went on to play Lizzie Spaulding in the CBS soap opera Guiding Light from 1996 to 2000.

For her role on Pixar's A Bug's Life, she was nominated for a Young Artist Award and Grammy Award, making her the fifth-youngest nominee for a Grammy.

Her other credits include Remember the Titans, Ally McBeal, Racing Stripes, Ice Princess and I Love You, Beth Cooper.

But it was her role as a cheerleader with superpowers in Heroes that propelled her to fame in 2006, with the series revolving around the mantra: 'Save the cheerleader, save the world.'

She won three Teen Choice Awards for the role.

Panettiere has also recorded a number of songs for the films and television programs she was in, including My Hero is You for the Disney Channel film Tiger Cruise and I Fly for the Disney film Ice Princess, which she co-starred in with the late Michelle Trachtenberg.

Panettiere has opened up about her struggles with addiction, beginning when she was just 15

Her first single not associated with an acting role, the reggae-infused Wake Up Call, was digitally released on August 5, 2008.

Clothing brand Candie's announced it was premiering an ad campaign for the single in late July of that year, and provided additional promotion for the song with a television ad and a music video starring Sebastian Stan, who played Panettiere's brother in The Architect.

Panettiere later played a brash country upstart opposite Connie Britton on Nashville, which aired on ABC for four seasons before being canceled and revived on CMT.

She did her own singing for the show, earning her some hits on the country charts as well as two supporting actress Golden Globe nominations.

In total, Panettiere had 11 songs recorded for Nashville appear on Billboard´s Hot Country Songs charts during the show's run, including two featuring Britton.

Following the news of her death, actor Randall Slavin shared a photo of him with Panettiere, writing: 'Peace be with you.'

She had shared the same photo just two weeks prior, with the caption, 'Good times and good friends.'

Actress Selma Blair also wrote on Instagram: 'I love you. Don't be gone. Don't be gone. Please,' while Melissa Barrera posted to her Instagram story: 'Rest in peace sweet Hayden.'

SAG-AFTRA added that it 'mourns the sudden passing of Hayden Panettiere.'

Sports.title: Arsenal look ready to dominate English football with the rest of the top teams in transition. And one player has been transformed by being a champion, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Until a team has finally crossed the finish line, there are always niggling doubts.

The psychological scars Manchester City had meted out on Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal over a period of three years were debilitating for this club.

It went beyond the ‘Second again, ole, ole’ chants or bottler jibes. It created a feeling that the men in blue were always just around the corner, waiting for the Gunners to slip up.

That imagery has been flung out the window. There is a confidence flowing through them after last season’s Premier League triumph and it augurs well for their upcoming campaign, which begins against Coventry at the Emirates on Friday night.

Arsenal just didn’t let up against City. When one goal came, the hunger for another superseded any thoughts to protect their lead.

In times before, going ahead so early on - 24 seconds into the game - caused the Gunners to panic or retreat.

Arsenal attacked Manchester City ravenously and served vengeance for years of coming second to Pep Guardiola

This is a different team, though, one emboldened to seize the moment of being on top, with the chance to be dominant in the months ahead. The rest of the 'Big Six' are going through transitions, remember.

Martin Odegaard typified this spirit the most. Having endured a stop-and-start season plagued by various injuries including to his knee and shoulder, the Norwegian hounded the opposition, desperate to make up for lost time.

Odegaard glided with a swagger which hasn’t always characterised him, transformed from becoming a champion.

He also played a number of incisive through-balls, constantly looking to pierce the opposition backline.

It wasn’t just his play. He pressed hard, not giving the forwards an inch on the ball. His goal on 48 minutes topped the display as he dumbfounded Josko Gvardiol and Gianluigi Donnarumma with just three touches.

It’s been some time before the midfielder has played in such a commanding manner, leading from the front in a real captain’s display.

When he’s confident and fully fit, Odegaard is a tricky player to face. He also sets the temperature in an Arteta team in sync around his intricacies. They rely on his pressing and ability to create chances in congested areas.

The calls for Declan Rice to take on the armband have festered in the background but here reflected just why Arteta has stuck with Odegaard.

Martin Odegaard played with more swagger now that he is a champion and was constantly forward-thinking

Arteta warned afterwards: ‘Well, he missed five or six months for different things (last season) and it was extremely difficult for him to get any momentum. If we can maintain him fit, available with the players around him, we're going to see a very different Martin.

‘I sensed from the first day he joined that he has something else in the belly that he wants to prove and show, because the team needs it as well.’

The substitutions sent a message, too. Having knocked the opposition off the park, Arteta brought on Declan Rice for the second half, and Bukayo Saka along with Piero Hincapie on 60 minutes.

There’s a depth to Arsenal which makes them an uncomfortable prospect to face when they’re on song.

The message is clear: the Gunners are firing and eyeing further silverware in the distance.

Gunners' new flying winger

The attention given to Arsenal’s pursuit of a marquee left winger had somewhat let £34million Christos Tzolis go slightly under the radar.

He was earmarked as a squad player, an attacker who would be knocking on the first XI door in seasons to come.

The 24-year-old, brought in to replace Leandro Trossard, already looks like a smart piece of business on the left side of Arsenal’s attack.

His headed assist for Kai Havertz after peeling away from a defender, or accurate pass to set Odegaard on the way to scoring, reflected why the Gunners brought him in.

He’s there to impact play, targeting goals and assists in a team without a 25 goal-a-season striker.

It’s now six goal contributions in six pre-season games for Tzolis. The Greek isn’t here to settle for a spot on the bench.

Christos Tzolis looked right at home against Manchester City, providing two assists

There is an opportunity to stake his claim - even more so if a pricey winger isn’t signed before the end of the window.

Thus far, he hasn’t put a foot wrong.

A telling trio of absentees

The Arsenal squad omissions presented an extra sub-plot.

Those left out included Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus.

Nwaneri has been the subject of interest from various clubs. So, too, has Martinelli, the subject of a £38million bid from Galatasaray. Jesus is edging towards a move to Napoli.

Of the three, Jesus is the closest to the exit door. Arteta played down the omissions, saying: ‘There's nothing to do with that (leaving the club). It's just a fact that we can bring 18 outfield players and we believe that for today's game, these were the options that we needed, especially with the physical condition of certain players.’

The players that Mikel Arteta left out ar potentially telling for the upcoming campaign

He added to TNT Sports: 'It's really sad to not have the availability (for them). I've been fighting with the Premier League to get more in the squad. Hopefully we can change that rule so players can be part of the squad. They're very important for us.'

All the same, their omissions pointed in a particular direction.

Sports.title: WNBA risks angering fans with Sophie Cunningham message as Fever star celebrates 30th birthday amid league's trans controversy
Sports.content:
The WNBA divided fan opinion with its social media post on Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham.

Cunningham turned 30 years old as the Fever defeated the Atlanta Dream 95-91 in a dramatic overtime thriller on Sunday.

The Indiana guard has spent the final few weeks of her 29th year in the headlines after sparking a debate on transgender athletes in the WNBA.

The league has recently been engulfed by controversy over transgender athletes after Sophie Cunningham said she wants to 'protect young girls' from 'biological men.'

Despite the uproar - during which the league declared that there were no issues with its eligibility criteria - the WNBA wished Cunningham a happy birthday on Sunday.

'Join us in wishing a Happy Birthday to 2025 Commissioner’s Cup Champion, Sophie Cunningham,' the league's official X account shared.

Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham celebrated her 30th birthday on Sunday

However, the message attracted backlash from some fans amid Cunningham's recent stance on the trans athlete debate with many claiming the league was monopolizing her for engagement.

'You won't protect her against hate, but you'll capitalize on her birthday. @WNBA is disgusting,' one fan responded to the post.

Another questioned: 'Oh now you like her when she can get you clicks?'

'The balls of the @WNBA for wishing her a happy birthday when they have attacked her and set her up for failure,' a third wrote.

'This post just lets you know that the WNBA is just milking this controversy for attention,' claimed a fourth.

Meanwhile, others took issue with the league sending well wishes to Cunningham as they seemingly opposed her stance on the issue.

'Not a chance. She’s a bigot,' one social media user bluntly replied.

'Yeah I’m done with the WNBA. Shameful organization,' added another.

The WNBA wished Cunningham a happy birthday on the league's official X account

The WNBA has been engulfed by controversy after Cunningham's comments on the participation of trans athletes in women's sports

Cunningham's stance has sparked uproar around the league, drawing both criticism and support alike. Two former NBA stars, Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White, declared themselves eligible for the WNBA draft in an apparent protest.

Freedom, who played in the NBA for 11 seasons and stands at 6ft 10in, announced his plans to declare for the WNBA Draft earlier this month amid the ongoing debate surrounding transgender athlete involvement in sports.

The former hoops star, who allegedly sent a provocative letter to WNBA commissioner, has sparked widespread criticism with his divisive decision.

Meanwhile, since his statement of intent, another former NBA star, White, has followed suit, also declaring for the WNBA Draft.

The 35-year-old, who only played three games in the NBA for the Sacramento Kings, told Fox News Digital that he is now transgender and wants to join the likes of Clark and Cunningham on the court next season.

White later doubled down by posting a picture of himself wearing a wig on social media.

WNBA general managers and presidents met on Wednesday as part of an anti-hate task force to discuss the subject of athlete eligibility amid the transgender debate.

Despite the uproar, the powers-that-be determined that there were no issues with its eligibility criteria, suggesting that no changes would be made.

WNBA chiefs, including commissioner Cathy Engelbert, met on Wednesday to discuss the subject of transgender athletes in the league

Ex-NBA star Enes Kanter Freedom has vowed to officially declare for the WNBA Draft in 2027

Royce White trolled his critics by posing in a wig and celebrating his 'feminine era'

The league announced following the meeting that it had ruled that there were 'no immediate eligibility matters affecting' the WNBA at this time.

WNBA chiefs also took the chance to address the recent storm surrounding the league, hitting out at 'bad-faith efforts' to 'marginalize others.'

'Today's meeting covered a wide range of topics, including ongoing discussions on transgender athletes and the continued hate and vitriol directed at players online,' a spokesman for the league said in a statement, via The New York Post.

'We will continue to engage all league stakeholders in the coming weeks and months. We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league.

'There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others.'

Currently, the league's collective bargaining agreement states that 'only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA,' but it does not include any more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

Some WNBA players and coaches have come out in support of transgender athletes, including Seattle Storm center Stefanie Dolson and Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve.

'We need to protect trans kids,' Reeve said on August 1. 'To me, it's a human rights issue. Every kid has a right to sports.'

Sports.title: Young, foreign and full of adventure... new Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli is everything his predecessor wasn't
Sports.content:
As is so often the case with managerial changes made in the aftermath of failure, Scotland appear to have turned on their heels and gone in a completely new direction with the appointment of Sebastien Pocognoli.

After the young Belgian was tonight confirmed as the national side’s next head coach, it’s clear the Scottish FA will be getting a man who could hardly be more different to his predecessor.

While Steve Clarke was experienced and pragmatic, but also dour and, well, Scottish, Pocognoli is a thrusting 39-year-old adventurer who will become only the second overseas coach in the country’s history, the first since Berti Vogts over two decades back.

Pocognoli and Clarke do have in common a passion for protecting and caring for their players, but this appointment is something entirely new for Scottish football’s governing body, who are recognising the nationwide appetite for change after this summer’s World Cup group-stage exit.

Yes, Clarke made history by taking Scotland to the finals of three major tournaments, but the Tartan Army ran out patience with his caution on the big stage and with his loyalty to players who were nearing, if not past, their sell-by date at that level.

And so, the SFA have sought to address those concerns with an imaginative appointment — Ole Gunnar Solskjaer is also reported to have been interviewed — whose profile, front-foot philosophy and touchline emotion will shake things up at Hampden Park.

New Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli will be an emotional presence on the touchline

Pocognoli's passion has prompted comparisons with Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone

Steve Clarke's caution on the big stage grew increasingly frustrating for the Tartan Army

Of course, it helps to tap into a fashion at times like these. Pocognoli’s biggest coaching success was at Union Saint-Gilloise, who benefited from Tony Bloom and his Jamestown Analytics empire long before Hearts. Don’t be surprised if ‘data-based’ gets a mention when Ian Maxwell and Mike Mulraney get round to explaining their rationale this week.

The season before last, Pocognoli made history by leading USG to their first league title since 1935. He also inspired them to a Belgian Cup triumph during a campaign that earned him the country’s manager of the year award. The club’s first-ever Champions League experience included victories away to PSV Eindhoven and Galatasaray.

All that earned Pocognoli a move to Monaco in October, but he lasted only seven months in the job. That was despite a 10-game unbeaten sequence and a run to the knockout playoff round of the Champions League, where they were pipped 5-4 on aggregate by Paris Saint-Germain.

He is an exciting proposition. While his coaching career is still in its infancy, he has already earned himself a reputation as a forthright, demonstrative coach, fiercely protective of his team and adept at psyching them up with stirring messages and disrespectful quotes from opponents.

Born in the Belgian city of Seraing, he is of Italian descent. Often dressed entirely in black, he is sometimes compared with the Atletico Madrid manager, Diego Simeone, although Pocognoli insists that the parallel extends no further than their personalities.

In an interview earlier this year, he said: ‘I am not calm. There is a lot of fire burning inside me — the Latin blood in my veins undoubtedly has something to do with that. My grandfathers were Italian.

‘I know about the comparison with myself and Diego Simeone. Simeone is a good coach, but he is not my great role model. Atletico Madrid’s playing style doesn’t appeal to me much either. At most, we share our Latin temperament.’

While Simeone is renowned for his teams’ counter-attacking strengths, Pocognoli takes a possession-based approach that features aggressive pressing and counter-pressing. After putting in place a structure that gives him peace of mind — 3-4-1-2 is his preferred formation — he wants players to express themselves. ‘I am very self-confident,’ he says. ‘I don’t doubt easily.’

On his arrival at Monaco from USG, Pocognoli was asked to elaborate on his principles. ‘There are two aspects: the collective and the individual,’ he replied. ‘My role is to establish a structure where the defenders are dependent on the work of the attackers. This is what my team did very well last year. This resulted in one of the best defences in Europe.’

As a player, Pocognoli performed well enough at left-back to earn 13 Belgium caps, although he never made it to a World Cup finals. He was involved when the country’s golden generation emerged, but he was also party to the regional factionalism that held it back. After a 4-2 home defeat by Bosnia-Herzegovina in 2009, he had a notorious dressing-room altercation with Timmy Simons and Stijn Stijnen, who accused him of not taking the result seriously.

Pocognoli started his playing career with Genk before joining AZ Alkmaar, where he won the Dutch title. After a move to Standard Liege and then Hannover 96, he had a three-year spell in England, notable mostly for his struggles at West Bromwich Albion. Out of favour with manager Tony Pulis, he went on to loan to Brighton before returning to his homeland.

The last days of his playing career were spent with USG, where he became coach of their Under-21s. That was followed by a spell in charge of Genk’s Under-18s and an age-group job with the Belgian national side before the big break came his way.

Even USG could not have imagined that, in his debut season as a manager in his own right, he would become the youngest in Belgium’s history to win a league title. Emboldened by that early success, he is hungry for more, inspired perhaps by some of the big names he has learned from.

Former Belgium team-mate Vincent Kompany is one of his role models. As is Louis van Gaal, the ‘most complete’ manager he has worked with. Pocognoli appreciated the Dutchman’s honesty when he played for him at AZ Alkmaar. ‘He taught me the most, tactically and technically. He had a very direct way of communicating, which shocked me a little at first.’

How Pocognoli, nicknamed ‘Poco’, adapts to international football should be fascinating. Will his limited access to players allow him to instil in them his distinctive way of playing? How will he fare without the recruitment that was crucial to his success in Belgium?

When he was a boy, Pocognoli wasn’t so keen on football and had ambitions to be an archaeologist. ‘I’ve always been interested in travel, culture, and adventure,’ he says. ‘Humanity inspires me. That’s what I love about my job: mixing cultures, learning from others.’

His next managerial experience will be an education all right. Let’s hope the cross-cultural experiment benefits Scotland as much as it does him.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish is still adored by Man City fans and staff but Community Shield cameo felt like a forlorn farewell, writes JACK GAUGHAN - and Enzo Maresca already has his wildcard option on their books
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish is still adored by Man City fans and staff but Community Shield cameo felt like a forlorn farewell, writes JACK GAUGHAN - and Enzo Maresca already has his wildcard option on their books

Unlock more from Jack Gaughan inside the Man City camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

The odds exceptionally lengthy, the name not on anybody’s bingo card. Maybe a quiz question in years to come, albeit a slightly tame one.

Jack Grealish was the first substitution of Enzo Maresca’s era at Manchester City, called during half time of what started as an abject afternoon and never recovered.

Grealish, the man with one Premier League start to his name for the club since December 2024, was out on the Principality pitch on his own as Maresca debriefed everybody else on a horrible first half inside.

Two members of the performance staff put him through his paces before set-piece coach James French emerged with an iPad. Presumably the message was to win some free-kicks, because City could barely lay a glove from open play.

And when Martin Odegaard poleaxed Grealish as he skipped beyond the Arsenal captain with an impish first touch, it felt like old times. But those are unlikely to return permanently. City are waiting for buyers, although one is unlikely to be Everton.

Grealish had started last season’s loan spell positively, with some even calling for an international recall after a string of assists, but his influence had waned before a stress fracture in his foot ended the campaign prematurely shortly after New Year.

A question mark looms over Jack Grealish's future - but on Sunday, he was the first substitute of the Enzo Maresca era

Man City are set to entertain buyers for the former England star but a reunion with David Moyes at Everton is off the cards

The Toffees have all but opted against going back in for the 30-year-old, shying away from a return after David Moyes had a sustained period of time working with him. There is interest from other Premier League clubs, although they are thought to have more pressing priorities in the transfer window. That indicates that an answer on his future might linger for a while yet.

‘Overall I think Jack was good,’ Maresca said. ‘The ones who are still here and want to work every day… if they deserve it, they're going to get minutes. At the moment the transfer window is open and we will see what happens.’

What Grealish’s introduction did indicate is the need for City to move in the market. Savinho – who is hopeful of pushing through a move to Tottenham - was not in Cardiff after being described as unwell when missing training in the week. With youngster Ryan McAidoo nursing a shoulder problem sustained during the pre-season tour of Asia, Maresca was without other options on the bench in that area of the pitch.

If Savinho does get his wish, the only natural, senior wingers on the books expected to have a true impact this season are Jeremy Doku and Antoine Semenyo, with City needing to sign reinforcements.

McAidoo will be given the chance to prove himself as a supplementary wildcard option, probably utilised in the cup competitions. Clearly not the immediate answer, despite undoubted talent. He has impressed the new manager with a direct style and willingness to beat a man one-on-one, something that Grealish rarely counts on. His best under Pep Guardiola came in acting as the integral ball carrier during the run to the Treble, winning fouls like the one committed by Odegaard or shielding possession, allowing City to pick their moments.

Academy youngster Ryan McAidoo will hope to prove himself to Maresca this season in cup ties

All the noises around how Maresca wants this team to play suggest that those skills are not necessarily top of the list of essentials required to flourish in this team. Grealish’s six-year contract finally expires next summer and it would be more likely that someone takes him on a temporary deal than permanent at this stage.

Grealish would have headed off on tour had he not suffered an injury, doing rehabilitation in Majorca with club staff – Real Mallorca also welcomed Elliot Anderson for a tune up – and then was back training with the squad over the past few days. England boss Thomas Tuchel visited his holiday home in the area around the same time as Grealish’s fitness camp.

City have changed their squad numbers, with Grealish wearing the No 18 these days. Rayan Cherki, the mercurial attacking midfielder who couldn’t hide his frustration at lacklustre displays from team mates in the Welsh capital, has taken the No 10.

There remains adoration for him, though. The loudest cheer of the afternoon from an understandably subdued City end came as the former Aston Villa captain trotted behind David Raya’s goal to warm up in front of them. There is still a great deal of warmth for somebody who will always go down in the pantheon, purely for his role in 2023, and a willingness for him to succeed.

That is the same at Everton, Grealish hugely popular with staff, but his career almost certainly lies away from both of those clubs now. It is down to somebody else to harness obvious talent that has not shone brightly enough for three years. It is down to him to recapture the love and dedication to the craft that remains in the locker.

It’s been missing for too long yet the way he longingly stared into the distance as Arsenal celebrated at full time did suggest that these days do mean something to him. The best result for City and Grealish is that a destination giving him both of those things is found sooner rather than later.

Sports.title: Amy Hunt makes history as 'track goddess' claims her FOURTH European Championships gold with Team GB mixed 4x100m relay triumph
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt makes history as 'track goddess' claims her FOURTH European Championships gold with Team GB mixed 4x100m relay triumph

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

With arms outstretched and a grin almost as wide, Amy Hunt signed off from these European Championships in the same way she began – by claiming a gold medal. Make that four in the space of a week and a slice of history.

No woman has ever won so many from a single sitting at this level, but a perfect week for Hunt was concluded by dragging Britain to victory via a tricky spot in the mixed 4x100m relay.

Added to a gold medal secured later in the evening by Georgia Hunter Bell, and team gold in the female marathon, it was stunning day for British women in Birmingham. But Hunt was the star. Hunt was the show. Hunt was the breakthrough act that offers rich promise for the second half of this Olympic cycle.

That much was shown again on closing night, in a new relay format that has the ring of a gimmick but leant itself to an unexpectedly tight race.

It started inauspiciously when Jeremiah Azu, the men’s silver medallist, left Dina Asher-Smith in fourth at the first change, before the former 200m world champion launched her team back into the lead with a superb leg of 10.04sec. But even then, there was work to do because Zharnel Hughes, surprisingly selected ahead of Romell Glave, lost the lead to Germany.

Enter Hunt. Taking the baton for the anchor leg, she was 0.03sec behind Gina Luckenkemper, but demolished that deficit in a handful of those long strides before seeing off the closing portion in just 9.86sec. Clocking 39.97sec, 0.14sec clear of Germany, Britain had another gold and so did Hunt.

Amy Hunt helped Team GB claim gold in the mixed 100m relay on Sunday evening

The self-styled 'track goddess' aimed for a historic four medals and won them without skipping a beat

‘Oh my gosh, I am over the moon,’ said Hunt, 24. ‘To finish it off with some of my best friends in the sport is incredible.

‘Me and Jeremiah have the same birthday, so we're kind of twins. To do it all together is incredible.’

Indicating that there had been a late change of plans to the line-up, Hunt also disclosed she had only practised handovers with Hughes an hour before the gun. Clearly they had the raw speed to cope.

While Hunt’s haul is unprecedented, it will be noted that the mixed relay was only introduced this year. But that will not be counted against a Cambridge graduate who destroyed all-comers as an individual in the 100m and 200m and has added two relay titles in the course of a single weekend. She once described herself as a ‘track goddess and academic badass’ and the counter-arguments are getting harder to stage.

The forthcoming intrigue will centre on how she competes at the World Championships next year, where the best of the United States and Caribbean might offer better perspective of her level. As for Asher-Smith, 30, this was the eighth European gold medal of her career and 11th of any shade, giving her the outright female record in the 92 years of the championship.

Less than an hour later, Hunter Bell secured gold of her own in the 1500m, with a victory that was easier to predict than any of the past week. With the exception of France’s Agathe Guillemot, no one in this field had ticked off the distance within three seconds of her best mark for 2026.

But it is one thing to stand apart on paper and another to dance through the tactical minefield of a race at the sport’s most complex distance. Hunter Bell’s approach was delightfully straightforward – she set a slow pace from the front and then kicked them all the smithereens in the final 300m when Klaudia Kazimierska attempted a challenge on the last lap. Crossing in 4:07.78, Hunt Bell was well over a second clear of the Pole in silver.

Hunt praised some of her 'best friends' in the sport - team-mates Zharnel Hughes, Jeremiah Azu, and Dina Asher-Smith

Georgia Hunter Bell blew away her competition with another faultless 1500m performance

For those who follow track and field, Hunter Bell’s story is well known by now, but fresh audiences ought to watch in awe of a woman who quit for five years in her twenties and only turned professional after Olympic bronze in 2024. Prior to that decision, she was working in cyber security; in the two years since, she has now seven international medals, including golds this season at the world indoors, Commonwealth Games and here. Remarkable.

The tone for British women was set earlier in the day, when Abbie Donnelly took bronze in the marathon – the first British female to ever step on that particular podium. Coupled with the elevated placings of Natasha Wilson (fifth) and Rose Harvey (14th), Donnelly led Britain to the team gold.

Jazmin Sawyers, competing two years after rupturing an Achilles tendon, took an impressive silver in a high-level long jump showdown. Her season best mark 6.99m was only bettered by Italy’s Larissa Iapichino.

Both the men’s and women’s 4x400m teams took silver, carrying Britain to 19 medals for the Championship, but the latter’s narrow loss to Italy gave the Italians top spot in the final table.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca admits Man City were 'not switched on' in dismal 3-0 Community Shield defeat and calls for transfers - while Mikel Arteta predicts huge season for Martin Odegaard after starring role
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca wants Manchester City to be active in the transfer market before their Premier League campaign starts on Sunday — after Barcelona finally agreed a £65.4million deal to sign Rodri.

City’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield laid bare the need for central midfield reinforcements, though a move for Lille and Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi is nearing completion.

Barca are finalising an agreement to land Rodri, who was not with Maresca’s squad in Cardiff.

‘Rodri is a player who just won the World Cup and Ballon d’Or,’ said Maresca before news of the agreement broke.

‘He’s a top player, all the teams need a player like Rodri, so it’s not about if we miss Rodri or not.’

City still hold an interest in Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez, despite the Blues’ Friday deadline to lodge a £120m bid having passed without a formal offer being made.

Enzo Maresca has called for more transfer activity after Man City's 3-0 loss to Arsenal in the Community Shield

Man City are closing on a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi, but Barcelona are expected to make another push this week to sign £70m-rated Rodri

‘He [Bouaddi] is still a Lille player,’ Maresca said of the 18-year-old. ‘Any new signing, the sooner they arrive the better because we are starting the Premier League in one week [City begin with a trip to Brighton on Sunday].

‘If they start to work with us as soon as possible it’s better so they can understand the way we want to play.’

Bouaddi — who was on the bench as Lille drew at Everton in a pre-season friendly on Saturday — wants to join City and the French club’s boss Davide Ancelotti confirmed there had been negotiations between the clubs.

Tijjani Reijnders is joining Al Qadsiah in Saudi Arabia for £52m after just one season at the club and Maresca admitted there is business City need to do if they are to compete for the biggest trophies again this season.

Elliot Anderson, Nico O’Reilly, Jeremy Doku and Erling Haaland all started the Community Shield, despite only returning to training in midweek.

‘Elliot was quite good for his first game,’ said Maresca. ‘We decided to start with four who had just two or three sessions.

ODEGAARD STEALS THE SHOW Mikel Arteta said Arsenal can use their Community Shield thrashing of Manchester City to lay down a marker to their rivals ahead of the club's Premier League title defence. The Gunners eased past Enzo Maresca’s men after first-half goals from Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz, before Martin Odegaard added the gloss on 48 minutes in a ruthless display. The north London club’s victory over the FA Cup holders gave them their second trophy in four months and their 18th Community Shield title overall, leaving Arteta purring. '(I'm) very impressed in the manner that we played, especially in the manner that we competed so that's a standard for us and if we have the standards at this level I'm sure that we're going to be really competitive,' warned Arteta. 'Probably there's more belief (after winning title), you know how to do it, you know what it takes to win it and the contribution of everybody because last season that was the biggest asset of the team. Every single player contributed to make us champions and we know that that's going to be exactly the same. ‘I'm obviously extremely happy with the performance, the results and winning the first trophy. We talked about the desire that we have to start the season and to show ourselves how much we want it, and I certainly saw a lot of positive things there against a top opponent.’ Odegaard stole the show as he led from the front after an injury-plagued last season. Arteta believes a different Odegaard will be raring to prove a point this time around. He added: ‘Well, he (Odegaard) missed five or six months for different things and it was extremely difficult for him to get any momentum, so I'm sure this year if we can maintain him fit, available with the players around him, we're going to see a very different Martin. ‘And I sense from the first day that he joined that he has something else in the belly that he wants to prove and show it, because the team needs it as well.’ ISAAN KHAN

‘The reason was because sometimes players prefer to start. The plan was to change all of them after 45 minutes, or an hour maximum.’

City started sluggishly, conceding inside the first minute, and Maresca criticised his team for not being ‘switched on’.

Captain Ruben Dias said the display was ‘frustrating’. He added: ‘It’s not good enough. Many things are changing, a new manager as well. If there is a lesson to be learned in a final, let it be this one because there are a lot more coming.

‘The most important thing is we’re already looking forward and we’ll be ready for our next game.’

Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Victor Osimhen statement made as Mikel Arteta drops next transfer clue

Galatasaray's stance on selling Victor Osimhen to Arsenal emerges

View 3 Images Galatasaray have addressed Victor Osimhen's future (Image: Getty Images)

The start of Arsenal's Premier League title defence is fast approaching, with the Gunners looking to get more business done before the big kick-off against Coventry. The Gunners have signed Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier so far, while Piero Hincapie's loan has become permanent.

‌



Arsenal's striker search has moved on to Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen, with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus potentially on their way out of the club before the end of the transfer window. Ethan Nwaneri and Martin Zubimendi could also depart before the September 1 deadline.

‌



Meanwhile, Jarell Quansah and Ezri Konsa have emerged as defensive targets as the Gunners wrestle with the absence of the injured William Saliba. The Gunners have seen at least one bid for Aston Villa's Konsa knocked back.

‌



Following Sunday's Community Shield final against Manchester City, Mirror Football brings you a round-up of the latest Arsenal transfer news…

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Osimhen statement made

Galatasaray have issued a strong 'hands off' warning amid Arsenal's interest in Osimhen. According to reports in Turkey, president Dursun Ozbek has told his inner circle: "I will not say 'yes' to any transaction that will harm Galatasaray or not benefit Galatasaray.

‌



Mikel Arteta sends clear transfer message to three Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield READ MORE :

"What I said about Baris Alper Yilmaz, I am now saying even more strongly about Osimhen. No matter how much the price is, I am not selling Osimhen."

Despite Ozbek's declaration, Turkish outlet Sozcu reports that Arsenal remain 'determined' to sign the Nigerian, who has also responded to the speculation over his future, saying: "There are always rumours during the transfer windows. I'll focus on my job. I'm focused on my work. We'll see and think about what comes next then."

View 3 Images Arsenal remain keen on Osimhen (Image: Photo by Burak Basturk / Middle East Images / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Arteta drops transfer clue

Mikel Arteta has dropped a clear hint that Nwaneri will soon be leaving the club. After being involved in pre-season, the attacking midfielder was omitted from the squad for Sunday's Community Shield against Manchester City.

Nwaneri's lack of involvement suggests he will be moved on before the end of the transfer window, with Galatasaray among the clubs interested in the youngster.

View 3 Images Ethan Nwaneri was in Cardiff but didn't make the squad (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Arteta addressed Nwaneri's future ahead of the Community Shield, saying: "I want him to be at the club but something is in the medium-long term what is best for the player as well. Ethan needs to play football and if he stays here it's because we can guarantee that he can have those minutes."

Arteta's selection for the first competitive match of the season suggests those minutes cannot be guaranteed.

Sports.content:
Luis Enrique gives frosty three-word reply as both Liverpool targets axed from PSG squad

Luis Enrique left both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye out of his squad for Paris Saint-Germain's clash with Lens on Sunday amid strong interest from Liverpool

View 2 Images Luis Enrique shrugged off the question post-match (Image: Ligue 1)

Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique wasn't in the mood to discuss the futures of Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye after leaving the pair out of his squad to face Lens on Sunday. PSG missed the chance to win a second trophy in five days, as they were beaten 1-0 by Lens in the Trophee des Champions.

‌



Barcola, who's valued at an eye-watering £145million, and Mbaye, valued at around £40m, watched from the stands at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis amid strong interest from Liverpool. The Reds are keen to sign both wingers in separate deals.

‌



PSG have this week brought in Ferran Torres and Mika Godts to strengthen their forward line, pushing Barcola and Mbaye down the pecking order. But even with their two new signings not ready to face Lens, Barcola and Mbaye weren't invovled either.

‌



In his post-match press conference, Enrique was asked about the decision and gave a short shrift. "Thank you, goodbye," the PSG manager replied before walking out of the media room.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Enrique wasn't best pleased after watching his side toil against Lens, who won the Coupe de France last season to set up a clash with Ligue 1 title winners PSG. Florian Thauvin scored just after the half-hour mark before Lens were reduced to 10 men before the break.

Kyllian Antonio saw red after a late studs-up challenge on Maghnes Akliouche, another forward who PSG recently signed. The hosts were forced to play with 10 men from the 39th minute onwards but held firm until the teams were balanced out.

PSG had a man sent off in the closing stages, as Nuno Mendes was given his marching orders for an elbow on Michal Skoras. Lens managed to see out the win and shocked the Champions League holders.

"When a player doesn't want to come here, or doesn't have a smile on their face about being here, it is better to find another solution."

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal rivals on notice after Man City win - 'We want to win everything'
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal rivals on notice after Man City win - 'We want to win everything'

Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard inspired his team to a fine 3-0 win over Manchester City to clinch the Community Shield - and then immediately set his sights on more silverware

View 2 Images Martin Odegaard insists Arsenal are coming for more silverware this season (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Martin Odegaard helped Arsenal humiliate Manchester City - before warning his rivals Mikel Arteta's men are on a mission to win everything this season.

‌



Arsenal swept City aside 3-0 to win the Community Shield in Cardiff, thanks to goals from Riccardo Califiori, Kai Havertz and Odegaard - his first in 2026. And Odegaard told the rest of the Premier League how champions Arsenal have the hunger for as many trophies as possible.

‌



Odegaard said: "We played some brilliant football. We showed our level. We showed we're ready, serious and want to do it again.

‌



"We want to attack it. When you get a taste of how nice it is, you want to do it again. We want to win everything."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arteta has now won two trophies in the last four months and he said: "I'm extremely happy with the performance. We talked about the desire we have - and to show how much we want it.

‌



"It's down to the preparation. I'm very impressed in the manner we played and competed.

"There is more belief. How to do it (win the title), and what it means. It makes a difference. I want to live those moments again. But we know it's going to demand something special."

This was Enzo Maresca's worst possible start to his mission of replacing Pep Guardiola. It was also his joint heaviest defeat as a manager in England.

‌



View 2 Images Odegaard and Kai Havertz celebrate Arsenal's killer third goal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC)

He said: "The big part of the game was the first goal we conceded. Then the second one made it more difficult.

"I'm always concerned, even when we win games. We have a lot of things we need to do better.

‌



"We will re-set, analyse the game and start thinking about the next one. We can find many things after this kind of defeat. We were not switched on."

Captain Ruben Dias insisted there was a lot of work for his side to do. He said: "It's obviously not good enough. It is a final that we all wanted to win.

"If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one. You need to push through and make things work between us.

Article continues below

"We need to keep on working. and there's going to be lots of challenges along the way."

Sports.title: Arsenal deliver painful Enzo Maresca reality check as Man City on end of mauling
Sports.content:
Arsenal deliver painful Enzo Maresca reality check as Man City on end of mauling

ARSENAL 3-0 MANCHESTER CITY: Enzo Maresca's first big outing since replacing Pep Guardiola turned into a nightmare in Cardiff as City's title rivals ran riot

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca endured a painful afternoon at the hands of Arsenal (Image: Glyn Kirk/AFP)

Arsenal dished out a mauling to Enzo Maresca in his first test since replacing Pep Guardiola. And a painful reminder to Manchester City of just how tough life is going to be without the Spanish genius.

‌



These two teams were the best in the Premier League last season. But in one game in Cardiff's Principality Stadium, the bitter rivals looked poles apart. Arsenal ripped City to shreds from start to finish, including an opening goal inside 23 seconds, on an afternoon Maresca will want to forget in a hurry.

‌



But the pressure on the Italian to maintain the incredible standards his predecessor set, will never escape him. As for Mikel Arteta, he waited three years to end his trophy drought, and has now pocketed two inside four months.

‌



Riccardo Califiori opened the scoring within half a minute - and Arsenal never looked back. Kai Havertz doubled the lead, before the impressive Martin Odegaard completed the rout in style.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

There was £125m worth of new talent on show, in the shape of Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Elliot Anderson, while Jack Grealish was named on the City bench.

‌



There was no Rodri for City, though, with the Spanish World Cup winner still at the centre of a transfer saga between his club and Barcelona. And it took Maresca's men just 23 seconds to miss the glue Rodri provides and come unstuck.

Miles Lewis-Skelly turned past Phil Foden and slipped a sublime pass inside Ruben Dias for Calafiori to run onto and beat Gianluigi Donnarumma with a neat finish. Welcome to the new job, Enzo.

Arsenal looked pumped up, and moments later Odegaard charged forward but somehow the move came to nothing, despite him having options left and right.

‌



City looked disjointed and sluggish. It took them 20 minutes to show signs of life, when Foden demanded a smart save from David Raya with a dripping strike. Gabriel had to snuff out a dangerous run from Jeremy Doku minutes later. The Brazilian then puffed out his chest and pumped up the crowd.

View 2 Images Arsenal ran riot to condemn Manchester City to a bruising defeat (Image: Getty Images)

It felt like this game meant more to Arsenal than City. So it came as no surprise when Arteta's men doubled their lead before half time. Odegaard picked out Tzolis at the back post and when he headed it back into the path of Havertz, the German managed to bundle his own header past a flapping Donnarumma.

‌



City had a mountain to climb. Scoring one past this Arsenal defence looked beyond them, let alone three. Especially when City started creating chances, but missed them. Erling Haaland should have beaten Raya, but saw his shot well saved, before Ben White produced a stunning block to deflect Doku's shot over the crossbar.

Califiori should have made it 3-0 at the opposite end, but volleyed over from close range, while Josko Gvardiol hacked a shot from Odegaard off his own line.

It got that desperate, Maresca sent on Grealish for the second half. But the first action he saw was Odegaard putting Donnarumma on his backside in the process of making it 3-0, to pile more pain on City. Maresca was taunted with chants of 'you're getting sacked in the morning'.

‌



Just one of the past 15 winners of this silverware have gone on to become champions that season.

But on this evidence, Arsenal look more than capable of bucking the trend.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement statement - 'It's all mapped out'
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement statement - 'It's all mapped out'

Cristiano Ronaldo has entered the last year of his contract with Al-Nassr after playing his final World Cup with Portugal, and the 41-year-old has opened up on his future plans

View 2 Images Retirement is near for Cristiano Ronaldo (Image: Stacy Revere/Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has dropped a bombshell and revealed that this season will 'probably' his last. Ronaldo, 41, only has one year left on his mega-money contract with Al-Nassr, having previously admitted that he's in the final knockings of his prestigious career.

‌



The Portugal captain played at his sixth and final World Cup over the summer, as his nation crashed out in the quarter-finals with a 1-0 loss against eventual champions Spain. Speaking for the first time since Portugal's heartbreak in an interview with Vogue Magazine, Ronaldo has suggested that this season will be his last.

‌



"This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy," he stated. "I have my future all mapped out. I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard.

‌



"Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one. And also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned - what we've earned. Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."

The interview took place five days before Ronaldo married his long-term partner, Georgina Rodriguez, in an intimate ceremony at their home in Cascais, Portugal. Earlier this week, the former Manchester United megastar returned to Saudi Arabia but didn't feature in Al-Nassr's opening game of the season.

The Saudi champions began their title defence with a 3-0 victory over Al-Fateh under new manager Ange Postecoglou. Their former boss, Jorge Jesus, left at the end of last season and is now Portugal's head coach.

Speaking at his unveiling press conference, Jesus said that the door was open for Ronaldo to receive a call-up, with their next match scheduled for late September. "I haven't spoken to Cris yet. He will never be a problem for the national team or for me," Jesus explained.

‌



Should Cristiano Ronaldo retire next year? Have your say in the comments section.

"As for the controversy, everyone is entitled to their own opinion. When the time comes to make a decision, I will speak with Cris and with everyone else individually. Cris is a symbol of Portugal. He will go down in history.

Article continues below

"It has been a great pleasure working with him. He is incredibly easy to work with. I need to speak with him to find out what he wants to do. He has always told me that he wants to finish his career at Al-Nassr. If he is in a position to be called up, I will do so."

Sports.title: Arsenal thump Man City to lay down early title marker and win Community Shield - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Arsenal gained an early psychological edge over old foes Manchester City by battering them in a one-sided affair to claim victory and the Community Shield.

In the first meeting between the two sides most heavily fancied to contest another gruelling title race, it was the Premier League champions who struck first - and within 30 seconds. Riccardo Calafiori finished with aplomb after rampaging forward from left-back after sterling work from Myles Lewis-Skelly, catching City cold.

Kai Havertz then made it two in the 28th minute, nodding the ball underneath the hapless Gianluigi Donnarumma after a smart blindside run and header back across goal from Christos Tzolis. Arsenal did need David Raya to be at his best to keep City at bay, while only a phenomenal block from Ben White prevented Jeremy Doku from halving the deficit despite the Gunners' dominance.

Three minutes after the restart, Mikel Arteta's put the game beyond City with Martin Odegaard showing excellent composure to sit down Donnarumma after being picked out by Tzolis.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Arsenal's fast start...and Lewis-Skelly's role in it

As far as dream starts go, it doesn't get much better than scoring inside 30 seconds. Manchester City were absolutely caught cold and left with a mountain to climb before some in sky blue had even settled into their seats.

Lewis-Skelly's role in the goal was significant; not only did he thread the perfect ball through to Calafiori in the City penalty area, he was also in the right place at the right time in his own box later in the half to prevent Nico O'Reilly from putting City right back into the game. This was another accomplished showing from the young Hale End graduate in his natural position. For sale? You can see why talk Lewis-Skelly could be sacrificed for superior financial flexibility has gone down about as well as a half and half Tottenham scarf with the Gunners fanbase. Surely there's a role for him in this team. If there was any doubt, maybe this display will give Arteta and the Arsenal hierarchy food for thought.

2. Tzolis keeps streak going

View 5 Images Christos Tzolis impressed against Manchester City and bagged two assists (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC)

‌



He may not have been signed to be the left-sided attacker to level up Arsenal's output from the flanks, but Tzolis has seriously looked the part in pre-season. The Greek international has registered a goal or an assist in every game he's played for his new club, a streak he extended here by teeing up Havertz following a smart run and pinpoint header back across goal. Not content with that, the former Club Brugge man picked out Odegaard in a crowded penalty area minutes after the restart to kill the game off.

With Gabriel Martinelli left out of the squad for the game, it seems a safe bet the shirt is Tzolis' to lose both for and following Friday's Premier League opener at Coventry. Yes, his cause has been aided by Arsenal's failure to land the marquee attackers they have been courting in the market. But Tzolis has looked every inch the superstar Arsenal have craved to enhance their left-hand side. All the while Arsenal are still scouring the market, he has a golden chance to lock down a starting berth.

3. City's Donnarumma dilemma

View 5 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma had a day to forget in the Manchester City goal (Image: Glyn Kirk/AFP)

More than a few eyebrows were raised when Manchester City signed Donnarumma just weeks after bringing James Trafford back to the club. Even more were raised when City doubled down on Donnarumma's status as undisputed No 1 after a mixed debut campaign by agreeing to sell the hugely promising Trafford to Leeds.

‌



Donnarumma was signed as one of the best keepers in the world. But while the man at the opposite end of the pitch continues to enhance his own claims for that honour, City's No 1 was absolutely all at sea. He was on the floor far too early for Arsenal's first goal, the second should never have squirmed underneath him and Odegaard sat him down the clincher third far too easily. Yes, even the elite are allowed an off day. But you do wonder whether Manchester City will harbour regrets over their decisions in the goalkeeping department long-term.

4. Grealish back in from the cold

View 5 Images Jack Grealish made a surprise appearance from the bench (Image: Glyn Kirk/AFP)

With Manchester City toiling, Jack Grealish was offered a surprise opportunity to take charge of his destiny when he was introduced as a half-time substitute.

The £100million man was frozen out and shown the door by Pep Guardiola but Enzo Maresca has refused to completely shut that same door when it comes to Grealish. His cameo here alone will not drastically alter his future. But if Maresca is open to giving him opportunities, perhaps Grealish and City's story could extend to a second act.

‌



5. Arsenal get early edge over rivals

View 5 Images Arsenal were comfortable winners in their first meeting of the season with Man City (Image: Charlotte Wilson/Offside)

In the grand scheme of things, neither Arsenal or Manchester City were ever going to put too much on today's game with the prize of the Community Shield smallfry in the grand scheme of things.

But a victory this comprehensive could give Arsenal a major psychological edge in the title race if, as expected, these two slug it out again for the domestic crown. Whether or not that proves to be the case remains to be seen. But this was not the polished first significant outing Maresca would have been coping for as Manchester City manager. Far from it. Arsenal on the other hand, were magnificent led by an inspired performance from their captain, Odegaard.

City will improve because of the talent they have, and because Maresca is a fine coach. But for now, it's Arsenal 1-0 Man City.
